title.zh: 卷一百八十三 列傳第七十: 王守誠 王思誠 李好文 孛朮魯翀 李泂 蘇天爵
title.en: Volume 183 Biographies 70: Wang Shoucheng, Wang Sicheng, Li Haowen, Bei Pailuchong, Li Jiong, Su Tianjue
title.raw: 卷一百八十三 列傳第七十: 王守誠 王思誠 李好文 孛朮魯翀 李泂 蘇天爵 Volume 183 Biographies 70: Wang Shoucheng, Wang Sicheng, Li Haowen, Bei Pailuchong, Li Jiong, Su Tianjue

sentences.zh: 王守誠

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng

sentences.zh: 王守誠，字君實，太原陽曲人。

translations.literal: Wang Shoucheng, courtesy name Junshi, was a native of Yangqu in Taiyuan.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shoucheng, whose courtesy name was Junshi, came from Yangqu in Taiyuan.

sentences.zh: 氣宇和粹，性好學，從鄧文原、虞集遊，文辭日進。

translations.literal: His bearing was harmonious and pure; by nature he loved learning. He associated with Deng Wenyuan and Yu Ji, and his literary skill advanced day by day.
translations.idiomatic: He had a gentle, refined presence and loved study by nature. Through his association with Deng Wenyuan and Yu Ji, his writing improved steadily.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，試禮部第一，廷對賜同進士出身，授秘書郎。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding, he ranked first in the Ministry of Rites examination; at the palace audience he was granted jinshi status with honors and appointed Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taiding reign he placed first in the Ministry of Rites examination. At the palace audience he received jinshi honors and was appointed a secretary.

sentences.zh: 遷太常博士，續編《太常集禮》若干卷以進。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, compiled several further volumes of the Collected Rites of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, and presented them.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, continued compiling the Collected Rites of the Imperial Ancestral Temple in several volumes, and submitted them to the throne.

sentences.zh: 轉藝林庫使，與著《經世大典》。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Superintendent of the Forest of Arts Repository and participated in compiling the Great Compendium for Governing the Age.
translations.idiomatic: He became superintendent of the Forest of Arts Repository and helped compile the Great Compendium for Governing the Age.

sentences.zh: 拜陝西行台監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor on the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 除奎章閣鑑書博士。

translations.literal: He was made Doctor for Appraising Books at the Kui Zhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was made doctor for appraising books at the Kui Zhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 僉山東廉訪司事。

translations.literal: He served concurrently as Commissioner of the Shandong Surveillance Commission.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently on the Shandong surveillance commission.

sentences.zh: 改戶部員外郎、中書右司郎中。

translations.literal: He was changed to Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue and Director of the Right Department of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to vice director of the Ministry of Revenue and director in the right department of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 與修遼、金、宋三史，書成，擢參議中書省事。

translations.literal: He participated in compiling the histories of Liao, Jin, and Song; when the work was completed he was promoted to Councilor of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in compiling the Liao, Jin, and Song histories. When the work was finished he was promoted to councilor of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 調燕南廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of Yannan.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to surveillance commissioner of Yannan.

sentences.zh: 至正五年，帝遣使宣撫四方，除守誠河南行省參知政事，與大都留守答爾麻失裡使四川，首薦雲南都元帥述律鐸爾直有文武材。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhizheng, the emperor dispatched envoys to pacify and comfort the four quarters. Shoucheng was made Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat and, together with Darimashi, the Dadu garrison commander, was sent to Sichuan. He first recommended that Shulü Duo'erzhi, Marshal of Yunnan, possessed both civil and military talent.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year of Zhizheng the emperor sent envoys to reassure the realm. Shoucheng was made vice administrator of the Henan branch secretariat and sent to Sichuan with Darimashi, the Dadu garrison commander. He was the first to recommend Shulü Duo'erzhi, the Yunnan marshal, as a man of both civil and military ability.

sentences.zh: 初，四川廉訪使某與行省平章某不相能，誣宣使蘇伯延行賄於平章某，瘐死獄中。

translations.literal: Earlier, a certain Sichuan surveillance commissioner and a certain branch secretariat chief councillor were at odds. The commissioner falsely accused the pacification commissioner Su Boyan of bribing the chief councillor, and Boyan died of illness in prison.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier a Sichuan surveillance commissioner had quarreled with a branch chief councillor. The commissioner falsely accused the pacification commissioner Su Boyan of bribing the councillor, and Boyan died in prison of mistreatment.

sentences.zh: 至是，伯延親屬有訴。

translations.literal: At this time Boyan's kin lodged a complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Now Boyan's relatives brought a petition.

sentences.zh: 會茶鹽轉運司官亦訟廉訪使累受金，廉訪使倉皇去官，至揚州死。

translations.literal: It happened that an official of the Tea and Salt Transport Office also sued the surveillance commissioner for repeatedly taking gold. The commissioner fled his post in panic and died at Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time an official of the tea and salt transport office accused the surveillance commissioner of taking repeated bribes. The commissioner fled his post in panic and died at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 副使而下，皆以事罷。

translations.literal: From the deputy commissioner downward, all were dismissed on account of the affair.
translations.idiomatic: From the deputy commissioner down, all were removed from office over the affair.

sentences.zh: 憲史四人、奏差一人，籍其家而竄之，餘皆斥去。

translations.literal: Four secretariat clerks and one memorial courier had their households registered and confiscated and were banished; the rest were all expelled.
translations.idiomatic: Four secretariat clerks and one memorial courier had their property confiscated and were exiled; the rest were all dismissed.

sentences.zh: 重慶銅梁縣尹張文德，出遇少年執兵刃，疑為盜，擒執之，果拒敵。

translations.literal: Zhang Wende, magistrate of Tongliang County in Chongqing, went out and encountered youths bearing weapons. Suspecting them to be bandits, he seized them; they indeed resisted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Wende, magistrate of Tongliang in Chongqing, went out and met youths armed with blades. Taking them for bandits, he seized them, and they fought back.

sentences.zh: 文德斬其首，得懷中帛旗，書曰南朝趙王。

translations.literal: Wende cut off one's head and found in his bosom a silk banner inscribed "King Zhao of the Southern Court."
translations.idiomatic: Wende beheaded one of them and found a silk banner in his clothes reading "King Zhao of the Southern Court."

sentences.zh: 賊黨聞之，遂焚劫雙山。

translations.literal: When the bandit faction heard of this, they thereupon burned and plundered Shuangshan.
translations.idiomatic: When the rebels heard of it, they burned and looted Shuangshan.

sentences.zh: 文德捕殺百餘人。

translations.literal: Wende captured and killed more than a hundred men.
translations.idiomatic: Wende captured and killed more than a hundred of them.

sentences.zh: 重慶府官以私怨使縣吏誣之，乃議文德罪，比不即捕強盜例加四等。

translations.literal: An official of the Chongqing prefecture, out of private resentment, had a county clerk falsely accuse him. They then deliberated Wende's offense, applying the statute on failure to capture bandits promptly with the penalty increased by four degrees.
translations.idiomatic: A Chongqing prefectural official, bearing a private grudge, had a county clerk frame him. They then sought to punish Wende under the statute for not capturing bandits at once, with the penalty raised four degrees.

sentences.zh: 遇赦免，猶擬杖一百。

translations.literal: Though an amnesty applied, they still proposed a beating of one hundred strokes.
translations.idiomatic: Even after an amnesty they still proposed a beating of one hundred strokes.

sentences.zh: 守誠至，為直其事。

translations.literal: When Shoucheng arrived, he set the matter straight.
translations.idiomatic: When Shoucheng arrived, he vindicated Wende.

sentences.zh: 他如以贓罪誣人，動至數千緡，與夫小民田婚之訟，殆百十計，守誠皆辨析詳讞，辭窮吐實，為之平反。

translations.literal: Other cases, such as framing people with charges of corruption amounting to thousands of strings of cash, and commoners' disputes over fields and marriage—nearly a hundred or more in all—Shoucheng analyzed in detailed judgments until their arguments were exhausted and the truth came out, and he reversed wrongful verdicts.
translations.idiomatic: In other cases too—false corruption charges running to thousands of strings of cash, and peasant disputes over land and marriage, nearly a hundred in all—Shoucheng examined each judgment in detail until the guilty confessed and he reversed wrongful convictions.

sentences.zh: 州縣官多取職田者，累十有四人，悉厘正之。

translations.literal: Among prefectural and county officials who had taken excessive official fields, fourteen in all were entirely corrected.
translations.idiomatic: He corrected fourteen prefectural and county officials who had taken more than their allotted official fields.

sentences.zh: 因疏言：「仕於蜀者，地僻路遙，俸給之薄，何以自養。

translations.literal: He therefore memorialized, saying: "Those who serve in Shu live in a remote region on distant roads; their salaries are meager—how are they to support themselves?
translations.idiomatic: He memorialized: "Officials serving in Shu face remote terrain and long roads, with meager salaries—how can they support themselves?

sentences.zh: 請以戶絕及屯田之荒者，召人耕種，收其入以增祿秩。」

translations.literal: I ask that abandoned households and fallow garrison fields be opened to cultivation by recruits, and that the revenue be used to augment official salaries."
translations.idiomatic: Let abandoned households and idle garrison lands be leased for farming, and use the income to supplement official salaries."

sentences.zh: 宜賓縣尹楊濟亨欲於蟠龍山建憲宗神御殿，儒學提舉謝晉賢請復文翁石室為書院，皆採以上聞成之，風采聳動天下，論功居諸道最。

translations.literal: Yang Jiheng, magistrate of Yibin, wished to build a spirit hall for Emperor Xianzong on Panlong Mountain; the Confucian schools commissioner Xie Jinxian asked to restore Lord Wen's stone chamber as an academy—all were adopted, reported upward, and accomplished. His bearing stirred the realm; in reckoning merit he ranked foremost among all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yang Jiheng, magistrate of Yibin, wanted a spirit hall for Emperor Xianzong on Panlong Mountain; the schools commissioner Xie Jinxian asked to restore Lord Wen's stone chamber as an academy—Shoucheng endorsed both and had them carried out. His reputation shook the empire, and when merit was tallied he ranked first among all circuits.

sentences.zh: 進資政大夫、河南行省左丞。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Grand Master for Governance and Left Vice Administrator of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to grand master for governance and left vice administrator of the Henan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 未上，母劉氏歿於京師，聞喪亟歸，遂遘疾，以至正九年正月卒，年五十有四。

translations.literal: Before he could take up the post, his mother Lady Liu died in the capital. On hearing of the mourning he hurried home, then fell ill, and in the first month of the ninth year of Zhizheng he died, aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could assume the post his mother Lady Liu died in the capital. He rushed home on hearing the news, fell ill, and died in the first month of the ninth year of Zhizheng at the age of fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 帝賜鈔萬緡，諡文昭。

translations.literal: The emperor granted ten thousand strings of paper money and gave the posthumous title Wenzhao.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor granted ten thousand strings of paper money and gave him the posthumous title Wenzhao.

sentences.zh: 有文集若干卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in several volumes.
translations.idiomatic: He left a collected works in several volumes.

sentences.zh: ○王思誠

translations.literal: ○ Wang Sicheng
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sicheng

sentences.zh: 王思誠，字致道，兗州嵫陽人。

translations.literal: Wang Sicheng, courtesy name Zhidao, was a native of Ziyang in Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Sicheng, whose courtesy name was Zhidao, came from Ziyang in Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 天資過人，七歲，從師授《孝經》、《論語》，即能成誦。

translations.literal: His natural gifts surpassed others. At seven he studied the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects under a teacher and could recite them from memory.
translations.idiomatic: His gifts were exceptional. At seven he learned the Classic of Filial Piety and the Analects from a teacher and could recite them by heart.

sentences.zh: 家本業農，其祖佑詬家人曰：「兒大不教力田，反教為迂儒邪！」

translations.literal: The family had long farmed for a living. His grandfather You scolded the household, saying: "The boy is grown—why not teach him to work the fields, yet instead make him an impractical scholar!"
translations.idiomatic: The family had always farmed. His grandfather You scolded the household: "The boy is grown—why not teach him to till the soil instead of making a pedant of him!"

sentences.zh: 思誠愈自力弗懈。

translations.literal: Sicheng only redoubled his effort and did not slacken.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng only applied himself all the harder.

sentences.zh: 後從汶陽曹元用遊，學大進。

translations.literal: Later he associated with Cao Yuanyong of Wenyang, and his learning advanced greatly.
translations.idiomatic: Later he studied with Cao Yuanyong of Wenyang and made great progress.

sentences.zh: 中至治元年進士第，授管州判官，召為國​​子助教，改翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Zhizhi, was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Guan Prefecture, summoned as Instructor at the Imperial Academy, and changed to Compiler at the Hanlin National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Zhizhi, was made assistant magistrate of Guan Prefecture, summoned as an imperial academy instructor, and then made a compiler at the Hanlin National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 尋升應奉翰林文字，再轉為待制。

translations.literal: Soon he was promoted to Attendant Drafter in the Hanlin, and again transferred to Academician in Waiting.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon promoted to Hanlin attendant drafter and later made academician in waiting.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，遷奉議大夫、國子司業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he was transferred to Grand Master for Discussion and Vice Director of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizheng he was made grand master for discussion and vice director of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 二年，拜監察御史，上疏言：「京畿去年秋不雨，冬無雪，方春首月蝗生，黃河水溢。

translations.literal: In the second year he was appointed Investigating Censor and submitted a memorial saying: "In the capital region last autumn there was no rain; in winter no snow; at the first month of spring locusts appeared, and the Yellow River overflowed.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was appointed investigating censor and memorialized: "Last autumn the capital region had no rain, winter brought no snow, locusts appeared in the first month of spring, and the Yellow River flooded.

sentences.zh: 蓋不雨者，陽之亢，水湧者，陰之盛也。

translations.literal: Lack of rain is the excess of yang; surging water is the predominance of yin.
translations.idiomatic: Drought means yang is overbearing; flooding means yin has grown too strong.

sentences.zh: 嘗聞一婦銜冤，三年大旱，往歲伯顏專擅威福，仇殺不辜，郯王之獄，燕鐵木兒宗黨死者，不可勝數，非直一婦之冤而已，豈不感傷和氣邪！

translations.literal: It is said that when one woman harbored a grievance, drought lasted three years. In years past Bayan monopolized power and favor, killing the innocent out of enmity; in the case of the Prince of Tan, and among the clansmen of Yantuemuer who died—the number cannot be counted. It is not merely one woman's grievance—does this not wound the harmony of qi!
translations.idiomatic: People say that when one wronged woman cried out, drought lasted three years. In recent years Bayan seized power and killed the innocent; the Prince of Tan affair and the deaths among Yantuemuer's kin are beyond counting. This is far more than one woman's grievance—has it not damaged the harmony of heaven and earth?

sentences.zh: 宜雪其罪。

translations.literal: Their crimes ought to be cleared.
translations.idiomatic: Their convictions should be overturned.

sentences.zh: 敕有司行禱百神，陳牲幣，祭河伯，發卒塞其缺，被災之家，死者給葬具，庶幾可以召陰陽之和，消水旱之變，此應天以實不以文也。」

translations.literal: Order the offices to pray to the hundred spirits, present victims and silks, sacrifice to the River Lord, dispatch laborers to block the breach, and for households stricken by disaster provide burial goods for the dead—then perhaps yin and yang harmony may be summoned and flood and drought dispelled. This is responding to Heaven with substance, not with empty form."
translations.idiomatic: Command the offices to pray to all spirits, offer victims and silks, sacrifice to the River Lord, send laborers to seal the breach, and give burial goods to families of the dead—then perhaps yin and yang may be restored and flood and drought ended. Heaven must be answered with deeds, not empty ritual."

sentences.zh: 行部至檀州，首言：「採金鐵冶提舉司，設司獄，掌囚之應徒配者，鈦趾以舂金礦，舊嘗給衣與食，天歷以來，水壞金冶，因罷其給，囓草飲水，死者三十餘人，瀕死者又數人。

translations.literal: On tour he reached Tan Prefecture and spoke first, saying: "The Gold and Iron Mining Intendant Office maintains a prison ward for convicts sentenced to penal servitude, who have their toes clamped to pound gold ore. Formerly clothing and food were provided; since the Tianli reign, floods ruined the gold works and the provisions were stopped. They gnawed grass and drank water—more than thirty died, and several more were near death.
translations.idiomatic: On his tour he reached Tan Prefecture and said first: "The gold and iron mining intendant's office runs a prison for convicts sentenced to penal servitude, with their toes clamped to pound ore. They once received clothing and food, but since the Tianli reign floods ruined the mines and the rations stopped. Prisoners gnawed grass and drank water—more than thirty died and several more were dying.

sentences.zh: 夫罪不至死，乃拘囚至於飢死，不若加杖而使速死之愈也。

translations.literal: When the offense does not merit death, yet prisoners are detained until they starve, it would be better to add strokes of the rod and let them die quickly.
translations.idiomatic: When the crime does not warrant death, keeping prisoners until they starve is worse than beating them and letting them die at once.

sentences.zh: 況州縣俱無囚糧，輕重囚不決者，多死獄中，獄吏妄報其病月日用藥次第。

translations.literal: Moreover, prefectures and counties alike have no prison grain; minor and serious prisoners whose cases are undecided mostly die in jail, while prison clerks falsely report the dates of illness and the sequence of medicines used each month.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover prefectures and counties provide no prison grain; many undecided prisoners die in jail while clerks fabricate monthly illness and medicine records.

sentences.zh: 請定瘐死多寡罪，著為令。」

translations.literal: I ask that penalties be fixed according to how many die of illness in custody, and enacted as statute."
translations.idiomatic: I ask that penalties be fixed according to how many die in custody, and written into law."

sentences.zh: 又言：「至元十六年，開壩河，設壩夫戶八千三百七十有七，車戶五千七十，出車三百九十輛，船戶九百五十，出船一百九十艘，壩夫累歲逃亡，十損四五，而運糧之數，十增八九，船止六十八艘，戶止七百六十有一，車之存者二百六十七輛，戶之存者二千七百五十有五，晝夜奔馳，猶不能給，壩夫戶之存者一千八百三十有二，一夫日運四百餘石，肩背成瘡，憔悴如鬼，甚可哀也。

translations.literal: He also said: "In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan the Dam River was opened, with 8,377 dam-labor households, 5,070 cart households supplying 390 carts, and 950 boat households supplying 190 vessels. Dam laborers have fled year after year, four or five in ten lost, while grain transport has increased eight or nine in ten. Only 68 boats remain, with 761 households; 267 carts remain, with 2,755 households—they rush day and night yet still cannot meet demand. Of dam-labor households 1,832 remain; one man transports more than 400 piculs a day, shoulders and back covered in sores, haggard as ghosts—most pitiable.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "In the sixteenth year of Zhiyuan the Dam River was opened with 8,377 dam-labor households, 5,070 cart households providing 390 carts, and 950 boat households providing 190 vessels. Dam workers flee every year—four or five in ten are gone—while grain shipments have grown eight- or ninefold. Only 68 boats and 761 households remain; only 267 carts and 2,755 households remain, yet they rush day and night and still cannot keep up. Of 1,832 surviving dam households, each man hauls more than 400 piculs a day, shoulders raw with sores, faces gaunt as ghosts—it is heartbreaking.

sentences.zh: 河南、湖廣等處打捕鷹房府，打捕戶尚玉等一萬三千二百二十五戶，阿難答百姓劉德元等二千三百戶，可以簽補，使勞佚相資。」

translations.literal: The Falconry and Hunting Offices of Henan, Huguang, and other regions have 13,225 hunting households such as Shang Yu, and 2,300 households of Arnaqa subjects such as Liu Deyuan—they may be drafted to supplement the labor so that toil and rest may support one another."
translations.idiomatic: The falconry offices of Henan, Huguang, and elsewhere have 13,225 hunting households such as Shang Yu, and 2,300 Arnaqa subject households such as Liu Deyuan—these can be drafted to share the burden."

sentences.zh: 又言：「燕南、山東，密邇京師，比歲饑饉，群盜縱橫，巡尉弓兵與提調捕盜官，會鄰境以討之，賊南則會於北，賊西則會於東，及與賊會，望風先遁，請立法嚴禁之。」

translations.literal: He also said: "Yannan and Shandong lie close to the capital; in recent years famine has spread and bandits run rampant. Patrol guards, archer soldiers, and officials charged with catching bandits summon neighboring districts to pursue them—when bandits go south they assemble in the north, when bandits go west they assemble in the east; yet when they meet the bandits they flee at the first sight of them. I ask that strict laws be enacted to forbid this."
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "Yannan and Shandong border the capital. Famine has bred bandits, yet patrol guards and bandit-catchers summon neighbors to pursue them—when robbers go south the pursuers gather in the north, when robbers go west they gather in the east—and at the first sight of the enemy they flee. Strict laws are needed to stop this."

sentences.zh: 又言：「初開海道，置海仙鶴哨船四十餘艘，往來警邏。

translations.literal: He also said: "When the sea route was first opened, more than forty Sea Immortal Crane patrol ships were stationed to warn the coasts back and forth.
translations.idiomatic: He also said: "When the sea route was first opened, more than forty Sea Immortal Crane patrol ships guarded the coast.

sentences.zh: 今弊船十數，止於劉家港口，以捕盜為名，實不出海，以致寇賊猖獗，宜即萊州洋等處分兵守之，不令泊船島嶼，禁鎮民與梢水為婚，有能捕賊者，以船畀之，獲賊首者，賞以官。

translations.literal: Now a dozen worn-out ships merely anchor at Liujia Harbor; though named for catching bandits, they do not actually put to sea, so that pirates grow bold. Troops should at once be posted at Laizhou Bay and elsewhere to guard them, ships forbidden to anchor at islands, townspeople forbidden to marry boatmen; those who can catch bandits should be given the ships, and those who capture bandit chiefs rewarded with office.
translations.idiomatic: Now a dozen broken ships sit at Liujia Harbor—they claim to catch pirates but never sail, so pirates flourish. Troops should guard Laizhou Bay and other points, forbid anchoring at islands, forbid townspeople from marrying sailors, reward successful hunters with ships, and promote those who capture pirate leaders.

sentences.zh: 仍移江浙、河南行省，列戍江海諸口，以詰海商還者，審非寇賊，始令泊船。

translations.literal: Orders should also be sent to the Jiangzhe and Henan branch secretariats to post guards at river and sea mouths, to interrogate returning merchants, and only when verified not to be pirates permit them to anchor.
translations.idiomatic: The Jiangzhe and Henan branch secretariats should post guards at river and sea mouths, question returning merchants, and allow anchoring only after confirming they are not pirates.

sentences.zh: 下年糧船開洋之前，遣將士乘海仙鶴於二月終旬入海，庶幾海道寧息。」

translations.literal: Before the grain fleet sails the following year, generals and soldiers should board the Sea Immortal Cranes in the last ten days of the second month and put to sea, so that perhaps the sea route may be pacified."
translations.idiomatic: Before the grain fleet sails next year, send troops out on the Sea Immortal Cranes in the last ten days of the second month so the sea route may be secured."

sentences.zh: 朝廷多是其議。

translations.literal: The court largely approved his proposals.
translations.idiomatic: The court largely adopted his proposals.

sentences.zh: 松州官吏誣構良民以取賂，訴於台者四十人，選思誠鞫問，思誠密以他事入松州境，執監州以下二十三人，皆罪之。

translations.literal: Officials of Song Prefecture framed innocent people to take bribes; forty persons appealed to the censorate. Sicheng was chosen to investigate. He secretly entered Song territory on another pretext, seized the surveillance commissioner and twenty-two subordinates, and punished them all.
translations.idiomatic: Song Prefecture officials had framed innocent people for bribes; forty petitioners appealed to the censorate. Sicheng was chosen to investigate. Entering Song territory on a pretext, he arrested the surveillance commissioner and twenty-two subordinates and punished them all.

sentences.zh: 還至三河縣，一囚訴不已，俾其黨異處，使之言，囚曰：「賊向盜某芝麻，某追及，刺之幾死，賊以是圖復仇，今弓手欲捕獲功之數，適中賊計。

translations.literal: Returning to Sanhe County, one prisoner pleaded without cease. Sicheng had his accomplices separated and made him speak. The prisoner said: "Bandits once stole someone's sesame; I pursued and stabbed one nearly to death. The bandits therefore plotted revenge. Now the archer soldiers wish to capture someone to fulfill their quota of merit—this fits the bandits' plan exactly.
translations.idiomatic: On his return through Sanhe County one prisoner would not stop protesting. Sicheng separated his accomplices and questioned him. The man said: "Bandits once stole a man's sesame; I pursued and nearly killed one of them, so they sought revenge. Now the archers want a capture to fill their quota—they are playing into the bandits' hands.

sentences.zh: 其贓，實某妻裙也。」

translations.literal: The stolen goods were in fact a certain man's wife's skirt."
translations.idiomatic: The supposed loot was actually another man's wife's skirt."

sentences.zh: 以裙示失主，主曰：「非吾物。」

translations.literal: Showing the skirt to the supposed owner, the owner said: "This is not my property."
translations.idiomatic: When the skirt was shown to the supposed owner, he said, "That is not mine."

sentences.zh: 其黨詞屈，遂釋之。

translations.literal: His accomplices' words were exhausted, and he was released.
translations.idiomatic: The accomplices' story collapsed, and he was released.

sentences.zh: 豐潤縣一囚，年最少，械系瀕死，疑而問之，曰：「昏暮三人投宿，將詣集場，約同行，未夜半，趣行，至一塚間，見數人如有宿約者，疑之，眾以為盜告，不從，脅以白刃，驅之前，至一民家，眾皆入，獨留戶外，遂潛奔赴縣，未及報而被收。」

translations.literal: At Fengrun County one prisoner, the youngest in years, was shackled and near death. Sicheng suspected this and questioned him. He said: "At dusk three men lodged with me, bound for the market fair; we agreed to travel together. Before midnight they urged us on. Reaching a grave mound, we saw several men as if by prior appointment—I grew suspicious. The group said they were bandits and told me to report it; I refused. They threatened me with bare blades and drove me ahead. At a commoner's house all entered while I alone was left outside; I secretly ran to the county, but before I could report I was seized."
translations.idiomatic: At Fengrun County a young prisoner lay shackled near death. Sicheng questioned him and heard: "At dusk three travelers asked to lodge with me on the way to market. Before midnight they hurried on. At a grave mound I saw men waiting as if by appointment and grew suspicious. They called them bandits and told me to report it, but I refused. They threatened me with blades and forced me ahead. At a farmhouse they all went inside while I stayed out, then I ran to the county—but was seized before I could report."

sentences.zh: 思誠遂正有司罪，少年獲免。

translations.literal: Sicheng thereupon punished the officials' offense, and the youth was released.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng then punished the officials, and the youth was freed.

sentences.zh: 出僉河南山西道肅政廉訪司事，行部武鄉縣，監縣來迓，思誠私語吏屬曰：「此必贓吏。」

translations.literal: He went out to serve concurrently on the Henan-Shanxi Circuit Commission for Upholding Justice and Purifying Government. Touring Wuxiang County, the surveillance magistrate came to welcome him. Sicheng whispered to his clerks: "This man must be a corrupt official."
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently on the Henan-Shanxi circuit commission for upholding justice. Touring Wuxiang County, the surveillance magistrate came to greet him. Sicheng whispered to his staff: "That man must be corrupt."

sentences.zh: 未幾，果有訴於道側者，問曰：「得無訴監縣敓汝馬乎？」

translations.literal: Before long someone indeed appealed by the roadside. He asked: "Are you not appealing that the surveillance magistrate seized your horse?"
translations.idiomatic: Soon a petitioner appeared by the road. Sicheng asked, "Are you complaining that the surveillance magistrate seized your horse?"

sentences.zh: 其人曰：「然。」

translations.literal: The man said: "It is so."
translations.idiomatic: The man said, "Yes."

sentences.zh: 監縣抵罪。

translations.literal: The surveillance magistrate was punished.
translations.idiomatic: The magistrate was punished.

sentences.zh: 吏屬問思誠先知之故，曰：「衣弊衣，乘駿馬，非詐而何！」

translations.literal: The clerks asked how Sicheng knew beforehand. He said: "Wearing shabby clothes yet riding a fine horse—if not fraud, what is it!"
translations.idiomatic: When his staff asked how he knew, he said, "Shabby clothes and a fine horse—what else could that be but fraud?"

sentences.zh: 陝西行台言：「欲疏鑿黃河三門，立水陸站以達於關陝。」

translations.literal: The Shaanxi Branch Secretariat reported: "We wish to dredge and cut the Three Gates of the Yellow River and establish water and land relay stations to reach Guan and Shaan."
translations.idiomatic: The Shaanxi branch secretariat proposed dredging the Yellow River's Three Gates and establishing land and water relay stations to reach Guan and Shaan.

sentences.zh: 移牘思誠，會陝西、河南省憲臣及郡縣長吏視之，皆畏險阻，欲以虛辭復命，思誠怒曰：「吾屬自欺，何以責人！

translations.literal: A dispatch was sent to Sicheng to convene surveillance officials of Shaanxi and Henan provinces and prefectural and county chiefs to inspect the site. All feared the peril and wished to answer with empty words. Sicheng said in anger: "If we deceive ourselves, how can we blame others!
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng was ordered to convene surveillance officials of Shaanxi and Henan and local magistrates to inspect the site. All feared the terrain and wanted to report empty excuses. Sicheng said angrily, "If we deceive ourselves, how can we blame others?

sentences.zh: 何以待朝廷！

translations.literal: How can we face the court!
translations.idiomatic: How can we face the court?

sentences.zh: 諸君少留，吾當躬詣其地。」

translations.literal: Gentlemen, wait a little; I shall go to the place in person."
translations.idiomatic: Wait here—I will go myself."

sentences.zh: 眾惶恐從之，河中灘磧百有餘里，礁石錯出，路窮，舍騎徒行，攀藤葛以進，眾憊喘汗弗敢言，凡三十里，度其不可，乃作詩歷敘其險，執政采之，遂寢其議。

translations.literal: The crowd followed in fear. For more than a hundred li along the river shoals and gravel banks, reefs jutted out in confusion; the path ended, they left their horses and went on foot, climbing vines to advance. All were exhausted, panting and sweating, and dared not speak. After thirty li they judged it impossible. He then composed a poem recounting the perils in detail; the chief ministers adopted it, and the proposal was shelved.
translations.idiomatic: They followed in alarm. For more than a hundred li along shoals and reefs the way ended; they dismounted and climbed by vines. All were exhausted and dared not complain. After thirty li they judged the project impossible. Sicheng wrote a poem detailing the dangers; the chief ministers accepted it and dropped the plan.

sentences.zh: 召修遼、金、宋三史，調秘書監丞。

translations.literal: He was summoned to compile the Liao, Jin, and Song histories and transferred to Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned to compile the Liao, Jin, and Song histories and made vice director of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 會國子監諸生相率為哄，復命為司業。

translations.literal: When the students of the Imperial Academy rioted together in a mob, he was again appointed Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When imperial academy students rioted together, he was again appointed vice director.

sentences.zh: 思誠召諸生立堂下，黜其首為哄者五人，罰而降齋者七十人，勤者升，惰者黜，於是更相勉勵。

translations.literal: Sicheng summoned the students to stand below the hall, dismissed the five ringleaders of the riot, punished and demoted seventy to lower quarters, promoted the diligent and expelled the idle—whereupon they encouraged one another anew.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng had the students stand in the hall courtyard, expelled five ringleaders, punished and demoted seventy to lower quarters, promoted the diligent and expelled the idle—and they began to encourage one another again.

sentences.zh: 超升兵部侍郎，監燒燕南昏鈔，忽心悸弗寧，已而母病，事畢，馳還京師侍疾。

translations.literal: He was promoted above his rank to Vice Minister of War and supervised the burning of worn Yannan paper notes. Suddenly his heart palpitated and he was uneasy; soon his mother fell ill. When the task was done he galloped back to the capital to attend her sickness.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to vice minister of war and supervised burning worn Yannan paper notes. His heart suddenly troubled him; soon his mother fell ill. When the work was done he raced back to the capital to nurse her.

sentences.zh: 及丁內憂，扶櫬南歸。

translations.literal: When he completed mourning for his mother he escorted the coffin south to return home.
translations.idiomatic: After completing mourning for his mother he escorted her coffin home to the south.

sentences.zh: 甫禫，朝廷行內外通調法，選郡縣守令，起思誠太中大夫、河間路總管。

translations.literal: Just after the end of mourning, the court implemented the law of universal transfer within and without, selecting prefectural and county magistrates. Sicheng was recalled as Grand Master of the Palace and Route Commander of Hejian.
translations.idiomatic: Just after mourning ended the court implemented universal transfers of prefectural and county magistrates. Sicheng was recalled as grand master of the palace and route commander of Hejian.

sentences.zh: 磁河水頻溢，決鐵燈幹。

translations.literal: The Cishui River overflowed repeatedly and breached the Tiedenggan embankment.
translations.idiomatic: The Cishui River flooded repeatedly and breached the Tiedenggan embankment.

sentences.zh: 鐵燈幹，真定境也，召其邑吏，責而懲之。

translations.literal: Tiedenggan lay in Zhending territory; he summoned its county clerks, blamed them, and punished them.
translations.idiomatic: Tiedenggan lay in Zhending territory; he summoned its county officials, blamed them, and punished them.

sentences.zh: 遂集民丁作堤，晝夜督工，期月而塞。

translations.literal: He then gathered civilian labor to build the dike, supervising day and night; within a month it was sealed.
translations.idiomatic: He then gathered laborers to build the dike, supervising day and night, and sealed the breach within a month.

sentences.zh: 复築夾堤於外，亙十餘里，命瀕河民及弓手，列置草舍於上，系木以防盜決。

translations.literal: He also built outer parallel dikes stretching more than ten li, ordering riverside commoners and archer soldiers to set up grass huts in rows upon them and tie timbers to guard against secret breaches.
translations.idiomatic: He built outer parallel dikes for more than ten li, stationed riverside villagers and archers in grass huts along them, and tied timbers to guard against secret breaches.

sentences.zh: 是年，民獲耕藝，歲用大稔。

translations.literal: That year the people were able to plow and plant, and the harvest was greatly abundant.
translations.idiomatic: That year the people could farm again and the harvest was abundant.

sentences.zh: 乃募民運碎甓，治郭外行道，高五尺，廣倍之，往來者無泥塗之病。

translations.literal: He then recruited commoners to transport broken tiles and repair the roads outside the city wall, five feet high and twice as wide, so travelers had no trouble with mud.
translations.idiomatic: He recruited laborers to haul broken tiles and pave the roads outside the city wall five feet high and twice as wide, so travelers no longer struggled through mud.

sentences.zh: 南皮民父祖，嘗瀕御河種柳，輸課於官，名曰柳課。

translations.literal: The fathers and grandfathers of the people of Nanpi had once planted willows along the Imperial Canal and paid tax to the government, called the Willow Tax.
translations.idiomatic: For generations Nanpi families had planted willows along the Imperial Canal and paid a willow tax to the government.

sentences.zh: 後河決，柳俱沒，官猶征之，凡十餘年，其子孫益貧，不能償，思誠連請於朝除之。

translations.literal: Later the river breached and the willows were all submerged, yet the government still levied the tax for more than ten years. Their descendants grew poorer and could not pay. Sicheng repeatedly petitioned the court to abolish it.
translations.idiomatic: Later the river breached and the willows were lost, yet the tax was still collected for more than ten years while descendants grew poorer and could not pay. Sicheng repeatedly petitioned the court to abolish it.

sentences.zh: 郡庭生嘉禾三本，一本九莖，一本十六莖，一本十三莖，莖五六穗，僚屬欲上進，思誠曰：「吾嘗惡人行異政，沽美名。」

translations.literal: In the prefectural courtyard three stalks of auspicious grain grew—one with nine stems, one with sixteen, one with thirteen, each stem bearing five or six ears. His subordinates wished to present them upward. Sicheng said: "I have always detested men who perform unusual policies to buy a fine reputation."
translations.idiomatic: Three stalks of auspicious grain appeared in the prefectural courtyard—one with nine stems, one with sixteen, one with thirteen, each bearing five or six ears. His staff wanted to report them to the throne. Sicheng said, "I have always hated officials who perform stunts to win praise."

sentences.zh: 乃止。

translations.literal: He therefore stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: He refused.

sentences.zh: 所轄景州廣川鎮，漢董仲舒之裡也，河間尊福鄉，博士毛萇舊居也，皆請建書院，設山長員。

translations.literal: Guangchuan Town in Jing Prefecture under his jurisdiction was the home village of the Han scholar Dong Zhongshu; Zunfu Township in Hejian was the old residence of the Erudite Mao Chang—all he asked to have academies built and mountain-chief posts established.
translations.idiomatic: Guangchuan in Jing Prefecture was Dong Zhongshu's home; Zunfu in Hejian was where the erudite Mao Chang had lived—he asked that academies and mountain-chief posts be established at both.

sentences.zh: 召拜禮部尚書。

translations.literal: He was summoned and appointed Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: He was summoned and appointed minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 十二年，帝以四方民頗失業，命名臣巡行勸課。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, because the people in the four quarters had largely lost their livelihoods, the emperor named eminent ministers to tour and encourage agriculture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year, because people throughout the realm had largely lost their livelihoods, the emperor named eminent ministers to tour the provinces and encourage farming.

sentences.zh: 思誠至河間及山東諸路，召集父老，宣帝德意，莫不感泣，緘進二麥、豌豆，帝嘉之，賜上尊二。

translations.literal: Sicheng reached Hejian and the circuits of Shandong, summoned elders, and proclaimed the emperor's benevolent intent—all were moved to tears. They sealed and presented double-crop wheat and peas; the emperor praised this and granted two vessels of finest wine.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng went to Hejian and the Shandong circuits, gathered elders, and proclaimed the emperor's benevolent intent until all wept. They presented sealed gifts of winter wheat and peas; the emperor praised him and granted two vessels of finest wine.

sentences.zh: 召還，遷國子祭酒，俄復為禮部尚書，知貢舉，升集賢侍講學士，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: Recalled to court, he was transferred to Chancellor of the Imperial Academy; soon again made Minister of Rites and placed in charge of the civil service examinations; promoted to Attendant Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: Recalled to court, he was made chancellor of the imperial academy, soon again minister of rites and placed in charge of the civil service examinations, then promoted to attendant academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while retaining the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 應詔言事：一曰置行省丞相以專方面；

translations.literal: In response to an imperial edict he addressed affairs: First, appoint branch secretariat chief councillors to administer each region exclusively;
translations.idiomatic: Answering an imperial edict, he proposed seven reforms: first, appoint branch secretariat chief councillors to govern each region;

sentences.zh: 二曰寬內郡徵輸以固根本；

translations.literal: second, ease levies in the inner commanderies to strengthen the foundation;
translations.idiomatic: second, ease levies in the inner commanderies to secure the foundation;

sentences.zh: 三曰汰冗兵以省糧運；

translations.literal: third, eliminate redundant troops to save grain transport;
translations.idiomatic: third, cut redundant troops to save grain transport;

sentences.zh: 四曰改祿秩以養官廉；

translations.literal: fourth, reform salary grades to nurture official integrity;
translations.idiomatic: fourth, reform salaries to sustain official integrity;

sentences.zh: 五曰罷行兵馬司以便詰捕；

translations.literal: fifth, abolish the traveling horse-and-troop offices to facilitate pursuit and arrest;
translations.idiomatic: fifth, abolish traveling horse-and-troop offices to ease pursuit of criminals;

sentences.zh: 六曰复倚郭縣以正紀綱；

translations.literal: sixth, restore suburban counties to rectify discipline;
translations.idiomatic: sixth, restore suburban counties to restore proper governance;

sentences.zh: 七曰設常選以起淹滯。

translations.literal: seventh, establish regular selection to raise the long-stagnant.
translations.idiomatic: seventh, establish regular selection to promote the long overlooked.

sentences.zh: 尋出為陝西行台治書侍御史，辭以老病，不允，力疾戒行。

translations.literal: Soon he went out as Associate Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat; he declined on grounds of age and illness but was not permitted, and forced himself despite illness to prepare for departure.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon sent out as associate censor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat. He pleaded age and illness but was refused, and set out despite his sickness.

sentences.zh: 十七年春，紅巾陷商州，奪七盤，進據藍田縣，距奉元一舍。

translations.literal: In the spring of the seventeenth year the Red Turbans took Shang Prefecture, seized Qipan, advanced to occupy Lantian County, and were one stage from Fengyuan.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the seventeenth year the Red Turbans captured Shang Prefecture, took Qipan, and advanced into Lantian County, only thirty li from Fengyuan.

sentences.zh: 思誠會豫王阿剌忒納失裡及省院官於安西王月魯帖木兒邸，眾洶懼無言，思誠曰：「陝西重地，天下之重輕系焉。

translations.literal: Sicheng met the Prince of Yu Aratnahiri and the provincial and court officials at the residence of the Prince of Anxi Yuelutiemuer. The crowd was alarmed and speechless. Sicheng said: "Shaanxi is a vital region; the weight of the realm hangs upon it.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng met Prince Aratnahiri of Yu and the provincial and court officials at Prince Yuelutiemuer of Anxi's residence. The assembly was terrified into silence. Sicheng said, "Shaanxi is vital—the fate of the realm depends on it.

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒，河南名將，賊素畏之，宜遣使求援，此上策也。」

translations.literal: Chaghan Temür is a famed general of Henan; the bandits have long feared him. We should dispatch envoys to seek aid—this is the best plan."
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temür is Henan's famous general and the rebels fear him. We should send envoys to ask for help—that is the best course."

sentences.zh: 戍將嫉客兵軋己，論久不決，思誠曰：「吾兵弱，旦夕失守，咎將安歸！」

translations.literal: The garrison generals resented guest troops overshadowing them, and deliberation dragged on without decision. Sicheng said: "Our forces are weak; we may lose the city at any moment—where will the blame fall!"
translations.idiomatic: Garrison commanders resented outside troops and debate dragged on. Sicheng said, "Our forces are weak—we may lose the city any day. Who will bear the blame?"

sentences.zh: 乃移書察罕帖木兒曰：「河南為京師之庭戶，陝西實內郡之籓籬，兩省相望，互為脣齒，陝西危，則河南豈能獨安乎？」

translations.literal: He then sent a letter to Chaghan Temür saying: "Henan is the hall and gate of the capital; Shaanxi is truly the barrier of the inner commanderies. The two provinces face each other like lips and teeth—if Shaanxi is in peril, how can Henan remain secure alone?"
translations.idiomatic: He wrote to Chaghan Temür: "Henan is the capital's gateway and Shaanxi its inner barrier. The two provinces are like lips and teeth—if Shaanxi falls, how can Henan stand alone?"

sentences.zh: 察罕帖木兒新復陝州，得書大喜，曰：「先生真有為國為民之心，吾寧負越境擅發之罪。」

translations.literal: Chaghan Temür had just recovered Shaan Prefecture; receiving the letter he was greatly pleased and said: "The gentleman truly has a heart for state and people—I would rather bear the crime of crossing borders and acting on my own authority."
translations.idiomatic: Chaghan Temür had just retaken Shaan Prefecture. Delighted by the letter, he said, "You truly serve state and people—I would rather face punishment for crossing borders on my own authority."

sentences.zh: 遂提輕兵五千，倍道來援。

translations.literal: He then led five thousand light troops and came to the rescue by forced marches.
translations.idiomatic: He led five thousand light troops to the rescue by forced march.

sentences.zh: 思誠犒軍於鳳凰山，還定守禦九事，夜宿台中，未嘗解衣。

translations.literal: Sicheng rewarded the troops at Phoenix Mountain, returned to settle nine matters of defense, slept nights in the censorate offices, and never once removed his clothes.
translations.idiomatic: Sicheng feasted the troops at Phoenix Mountain, settled nine points of defense, and slept in the censorate offices without undressing.

sentences.zh: 同官潛送妻子過渭北，思誠止之。

translations.literal: Colleagues secretly sent wives and children north of the Wei; Sicheng stopped them.
translations.idiomatic: Colleagues secretly sent their families north of the Wei; Sicheng stopped them.

sentences.zh: 分守北門，其屬聞事急，欲圖苟免，思誠從容諭之曰：「吾受國重寄，安定一方，期戮力報效，死之可也。

translations.literal: He was assigned to guard the north gate. His subordinates, hearing matters urgent, wished to seek a way out. Sicheng calmly instructed them: "I bear the state's heavy trust to secure this region and expect to exert our strength in loyal service—death is acceptable.
translations.idiomatic: Assigned to guard the north gate, his subordinates heard how grave matters were and sought escape. Sicheng calmly told them, "The state has entrusted me to secure this region—we must serve with all our strength, and death is acceptable.

sentences.zh: 自古皆有死，在遲與速耳。」

translations.literal: From antiquity all men die—the difference is only sooner or later."
translations.idiomatic: All men die since antiquity—only the timing differs."

sentences.zh: 眾乃安。

translations.literal: The crowd was then reassured.
translations.idiomatic: The men were reassured.

sentences.zh: 既而援兵破賊，河南總兵官果以察罕帖木兒擅調，遣人問之，思誠亟請於朝，宜命察罕帖木兒專守關陝，仍令便宜行事，詔從之。

translations.literal: Before long the relief troops defeated the bandits. The Henan commander-in-chief indeed questioned Chaghan Temür for unauthorized transfer of troops. Sicheng urgently petitioned the court that Chaghan Temür should be ordered to guard Guan and Shaan exclusively and still be permitted discretionary action; an edict followed his request.
translations.idiomatic: Relief troops soon defeated the rebels. The Henan commander questioned Chaghan Temür for unauthorized troop movement. Sicheng urgently asked the court to put him in charge of Guan and Shaan with discretionary authority; the edict followed.

sentences.zh: 行樞密院掾史田甲，受賂事覺，匿豫邸，監察御史捕之急，並係其母，思誠過市中，見之，曰：「嘻！

translations.literal: Tian Jia, a clerk of the Traveling Privy Council, was discovered taking bribes and hid in the Prince of Yu's residence. Investigating censors pressed the arrest and also bound his mother. Sicheng passed through the market, saw this, and said: "Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Tian Jia, a clerk of the traveling privy council, was caught taking bribes and hid in the Prince of Yu's residence. Censors pressed the arrest and also bound his mother. Passing through the market, Sicheng exclaimed, "Alas!

sentences.zh: 古者罪人不孥，況其母乎！

translations.literal: In antiquity punishment did not extend to a criminal's family—how much more his mother!
translations.idiomatic: In antiquity guilt did not extend to kin—how much less to a mother!

sentences.zh: 吾不忍以子而係其母。」

translations.literal: I cannot bear to bind a mother because of her son."
translations.idiomatic: I cannot bear to bind a mother because of her son."

sentences.zh: 令釋之，不從，思誠因自劾不出，諸御史謁而謝之。

translations.literal: He ordered her released; they did not comply. Sicheng therefore impeached himself and refused to attend office; the censors called on him and apologized.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered her released, but they refused. Sicheng impeached himself and stayed away from office until the censors came to apologize.

sentences.zh: 初，監察御史有封事，自中丞以下，惟署紙尾，莫敢問其由，事行，始知之，思誠曰：「若是，則上下之分安在！」

translations.literal: Earlier, when investigating censors had sealed memorials, from the vice censor-in-chief downward they only signed the end of the paper and dared not ask the reason; only when the matter was executed did they learn of it. Sicheng said: "If it is thus, where is the distinction between superior and subordinate!"
translations.idiomatic: Earlier sealed memorials from investigating censors were signed only at the end by the vice censor-in-chief down, with no one daring to ask the contents until action was taken. Sicheng said, "If that is so, what becomes of hierarchy?"

sentences.zh: 凡上章，必拆視，不可行者，以台印封置架閣庫。

translations.literal: Henceforth every memorial submitted must be opened and read; those that could not be carried out were sealed with the censorate seal and placed in the archive.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter every memorial had to be opened and read; unacceptable ones were sealed with the censorate seal and filed in the archive.

sentences.zh: 俄起五省餘丁軍，思誠爭曰：「關中方用兵，困於供給，民多愁怨，復有是役，萬一為變，所繫豈輕耶！」

translations.literal: Soon a levy was raised for surplus-man troops of the five provinces. Sicheng protested: "Guanzhong is already at war, straitened in supplies, and the people are full of grievance—if this labor is added and rebellion should arise, is what hangs in the balance slight!"
translations.idiomatic: Soon a levy was raised for surplus-man troops from five provinces. Sicheng protested, "Guanzhong is already at war, supplies are strained, and the people are bitter—if this levy sparks revolt, the consequences will be grave!"

sentences.zh: 事遂寢。

translations.literal: The matter was then shelved.
translations.idiomatic: The project was dropped.

sentences.zh: 十七年，召拜通議大夫、國子祭酒，時臥疾，聞命即起，至朝邑，疾復作。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was summoned and appointed Grand Master for Discussion and Chancellor of the Imperial Academy. Though then bedridden with illness, on hearing the appointment he rose at once; reaching Chaoyi his illness recurred.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he was summoned as grand master for discussion and chancellor of the imperial academy. Though ill in bed, he rose on hearing the order; at Chaoyi his illness returned.

sentences.zh: 十月，卒於旅舍，年六十有七。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he died at an inn, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he died at an inn at the age of sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 諡獻肅。

translations.literal: He was given the posthumous title Xiansu.
translations.idiomatic: He was given the posthumous title Xiansu.

sentences.zh: ○李好文

translations.literal: ○ Li Haowen
translations.idiomatic: Li Haowen

sentences.zh: 李好文，字惟中，大名之東明人。

translations.literal: Li Haowen, courtesy name Weizhong, was a native of Dongming in Daming.
translations.idiomatic: Li Haowen, whose courtesy name was Weizhong, came from Dongming in Daming.

sentences.zh: 登至治元年進士第，授大名路浚州判官。

translations.literal: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Zhizhi and was appointed Assistant Magistrate of Jun Prefecture on the Daming Route.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the jinshi examination in the first year of Zhizhi and was made assistant magistrate of Jun Prefecture on the Daming route.

sentences.zh: 入為翰林國史院編修官、國子助教。

translations.literal: He entered service as Compiler at the Hanlin National History Institute and Instructor at the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He entered service as a Hanlin national history compiler and imperial academy instructor.

sentences.zh: 泰定四年，除太常博士。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Taiding he was made Doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Taiding he was made doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 會盜竊太廟神主，好文言：「在禮，神主當以木為之，金玉祭器，宜貯之別室。」

translations.literal: When thieves stole the spirit tablets of the Imperial Ancestral Temple, Haowen said: "According to ritual, spirit tablets should be made of wood; gold and jade sacrificial vessels should be stored in a separate chamber."
translations.idiomatic: When thieves stole the imperial ancestral temple spirit tablets, Haowen said, "By ritual, spirit tablets should be wood; gold and jade vessels should be kept in a separate chamber."

sentences.zh: 又言：「祖宗建國以來，七八十年，每遇大禮，皆臨時取具，博士不過循故事應答而已。

translations.literal: He also said: "Since the founding of the state by our ancestors, for seven or eight decades, whenever great rites occurred everything was gathered at the last moment; the doctors merely followed precedent in reply—that was all.
translations.idiomatic: He also said, "For seven or eight decades since the founding, every great rite has been equipped at the last moment, and temple doctors have only repeated precedent.

sentences.zh: 往年有詔為《集禮》，而乃令各省及各郡縣置局纂修，宜其久不成也。

translations.literal: In years past there was an edict to compile the Collected Rites, yet provinces and every prefecture and county were ordered to set up bureaus to compile and revise—no wonder it long remained unfinished.
translations.idiomatic: An edict once ordered compilation of the Collected Rites, yet every province, prefecture, and county was told to set up a bureau—no wonder it never finished.

sentences.zh: 禮樂自朝廷出，郡縣何有哉！」

translations.literal: Rites and music proceed from the court—what have prefectures and counties to do with them!"
translations.idiomatic: Rites and music come from the court—what business have prefectures and counties with them!"

sentences.zh: 白長院者，選僚屬數人，仍請出架閣文牘，以資採錄。

translations.literal: He informed the chief of the institute, selected several subordinates, and also asked that archive documents be produced for collection and transcription.
translations.idiomatic: He informed the institute chief, chose several aides, and asked for archive documents to compile from.

sentences.zh: 三年，書成，凡五十卷，名曰《太常集禮》。

translations.literal: In three years the book was completed, fifty volumes in all, entitled Collected Rites of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: In three years the work was finished—fifty volumes entitled Collected Rites of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 遷國子博士。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Doctor of the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to doctor of the imperial academy.

sentences.zh: 丁內憂，服闋，起為國子監丞，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: He completed mourning for his mother; when mourning ended he was recalled as Vice Director of the Imperial Academy and appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for his mother he was recalled as vice director of the imperial academy and appointed investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 時復以至元紀元，好文言：「年號襲舊，於古未聞，襲其名而不蹈其實，未見其益。」

translations.literal: At the time the Zhiyuan reign title was revived. Haowen said: "To reuse an old era name is unheard of in antiquity; to take its name without following its substance—I see no benefit."
translations.idiomatic: When the Zhiyuan reign title was revived, Haowen said, "Reusing an old era name is unheard of in antiquity; taking the name without its substance brings no benefit."

sentences.zh: 因言時弊不如至元者十餘事。

translations.literal: He then cited more than ten current abuses inferior to the Zhiyuan period.
translations.idiomatic: He then listed more than ten current abuses worse than under Zhiyuan.

sentences.zh: 錄囚河東，有李拜拜者，殺人，而行凶之仗不明，凡十四年不決，好文曰：「豈有不決之獄如是其久乎！」

translations.literal: Reviewing prisoners in Hedong, there was one Li Baibai who had killed a man, yet the weapon used was unclear; for fourteen years the case was undecided. Haowen said: "Can there be an undecided case lasting so long!"
translations.idiomatic: Reviewing prisoners in Hedong, he found Li Baibai, accused of murder with the weapon unclear, undecided for fourteen years. Haowen said, "Can a case remain undecided so long?"

sentences.zh: 立出之。

translations.literal: He had him released at once.
translations.idiomatic: He had him released at once.

sentences.zh: 王傅撒都剌，以足蹋人而死，眾皆曰：「殺人非刃，當杖之。」

translations.literal: The prince's tutor Sadula kicked a man to death. All said: "Killing without a blade should be punished by beating."
translations.idiomatic: The prince's tutor Sadula kicked a man to death. All said killing without a blade should be punished by beating.

sentences.zh: 好文曰：「怙勢殺人，甚於用刃，況因有所求而殺之，其情為尤重。」

translations.literal: Haowen said: "Relying on power to kill is worse than using a blade—how much more when one kills to obtain something; the circumstances are especially grave."
translations.idiomatic: Haowen said, "Killing by abuse of power is worse than with a blade—especially when done to obtain something; the crime is graver still."

sentences.zh: 乃置之死，河東為之震肅。

translations.literal: He therefore sentenced him to death, and Hedong was shaken into awe.
translations.idiomatic: He sentenced him to death, and Hedong was awed into order.

sentences.zh: 出僉河南、浙東兩道廉訪司事。

translations.literal: He went out to serve concurrently on the Henan and Zhedong surveillance commissions.
translations.idiomatic: He served concurrently on the Henan and Zhedong surveillance commissions.

sentences.zh: 六年，帝親享太室，召僉太常禮儀院事。

translations.literal: In the sixth year the emperor personally offered in the Grand Chamber; Haowen was summoned to serve concurrently as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Ritual Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year the emperor personally offered in the Grand Chamber and summoned Haowen to serve concurrently on the imperial ancestral temple and ritual institute.

sentences.zh: 至正元年，除國子祭酒，改陝西行台治書侍御史，遷河東道廉訪使。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhizheng he was made Chancellor of the Imperial Academy, changed to Associate Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and transferred to Surveillance Commissioner of the Hedong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Zhizheng he was made chancellor of the imperial academy, then associate censor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat, then surveillance commissioner of the Hedong circuit.

sentences.zh: 三年，郊祀，召為同知太常禮儀院事。

translations.literal: In the third year, at the suburban sacrifice, he was summoned as Vice Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Ritual Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year, at the suburban sacrifice, he was summoned as vice director of the imperial ancestral temple and ritual institute.

sentences.zh: 帝之親祀也，至寧宗室，遣阿魯問曰：「兄拜弟可乎？」

translations.literal: When the emperor performed the sacrifice in person and reached the chamber of Emperor Ningzong, he sent Aru to ask: "May an elder brother bow to a younger brother?"
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor sacrificed in person and reached Emperor Ningzong's tablet, he sent Aru to ask, "May an elder brother bow to a younger brother?"

sentences.zh: 好文與博士劉聞對曰：「為人後者，為之子也。」

translations.literal: Haowen and the doctor Liu Wen replied: "One who becomes another's heir stands as his son."
translations.idiomatic: Haowen and the doctor Liu Wen replied, "An adopted heir stands as a son."

sentences.zh: 帝遂拜。

translations.literal: The emperor then bowed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor bowed.

sentences.zh: 由是每親祀，必命好文攝禮儀使。

translations.literal: From this, whenever the emperor sacrificed in person, Haowen was always ordered to act as ritual commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter whenever the emperor sacrificed in person, Haowen was appointed acting ritual commissioner.

sentences.zh: 四年，除江南行台治書侍御史，未行，改禮部尚書，與修遼、金、宋史，除治書侍御史，仍與史事。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was made Associate Censor of the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat; before departing he was changed to Minister of Rites and joined in compiling the Liao, Jin, and Song histories; he was then made Associate Censor while still engaged in the histories.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was made associate censor of the Jiangnan branch secretariat but before leaving was made minister of rites and joined compiling the Liao, Jin, and Song histories, then made associate censor while still working on the histories.

sentences.zh: 俄除參議中書省事，視事十日，以史故，仍為治書。

translations.literal: Soon he was made Councilor of the Secretariat; after ten days in office, on account of the histories, he again became associate censor.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was made councilor of the Secretariat, but after ten days returned to associate censor because of the histories.

sentences.zh: 已而復除陝西行台治書侍御史，時台臣皆缺，好文獨署台事。

translations.literal: Before long he was again made Associate Censor of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat. At the time censorate posts were all vacant; Haowen alone signed censorate business.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made associate censor of the Shaanxi branch secretariat. With all censorate posts vacant, Haowen alone handled its affairs.

sentences.zh: 西蜀奉使，以私憾摭拾廉訪使曾文博、僉事兀馬兒、王武事，文博死，兀馬兒誣服，武不屈，以輕侮抵罪。

translations.literal: An envoy to Western Shu, out of private resentment, gathered charges against Surveillance Commissioner Zeng Wenbo, Commissioner Wuma'er, and Wang Wu. Wenbo died; Wuma'er confessed under false accusation; Wu would not yield and was punished for contempt.
translations.idiomatic: An envoy to Western Shu, bearing a private grudge, framed surveillance commissioner Zeng Wenbo, commissioner Wuma'er, and Wang Wu. Wenbo died; Wuma'er confessed under duress; Wu refused and was punished for contempt.

sentences.zh: 好文曰：「奉使代天子行事，當問民疾苦，黜陟邪正，今行省以下，至於郡縣，未聞舉劾一人，獨風憲之司，無一免者，此豈正大之體乎！」

translations.literal: Haowen said: "An envoy acts for the Son of Heaven and should inquire into the people's hardships and promote the upright while removing the corrupt. From branch secretariats down to prefectures and counties, not one person has been impeached—only the surveillance offices, and none escape. Is this the upright way!"
translations.idiomatic: Haowen said, "An envoy acts for the Son of Heaven and should inquire into people's hardships and reward the upright while removing the corrupt. From branch secretariats down to counties, not one official has been impeached—only surveillance officials, and none escape. Is that upright governance?"

sentences.zh: 率御史力辨武等之枉，並言奉使不法者十餘事。

translations.literal: He led the censors in forcefully arguing the injustice done to Wu and others, and also reported more than ten unlawful acts of the envoy.
translations.idiomatic: He led the censors in vindicating Wu and others and reported more than ten unlawful acts by the envoy.

sentences.zh: 六年，除翰林侍講學士，兼國子祭酒，又遷改集賢侍講學士，仍兼祭酒。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was made Hanlin Academician Explaining the Classics, concurrently Chancellor of the Imperial Academy; he was again transferred to Attendant Academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies, still concurrently chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was made Hanlin lecturing academician and concurrent chancellor of the imperial academy, then transferred to attendant academician of the Hall of Gathered Worthies while retaining the chancellorship.

sentences.zh: 九年，出參湖廣行省政事，改湖北道廉訪使，尋召為太常禮儀院使。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he went out as Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, was changed to Surveillance Commissioner of the Hubei Circuit, and soon summoned as Director of the Imperial Ancestral Temple and Ritual Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he served as administrator of the Huguang branch secretariat, then surveillance commissioner of the Hubei circuit, and was soon summoned as director of the imperial ancestral temple and ritual institute.

sentences.zh: 於是帝以皇太子年漸長，開端本堂，命皇太子入學，以右丞相脫脫、大司徒雅不花知端本堂事，而命好文以翰林學士兼諭德。

translations.literal: Thereupon, as the crown prince grew older, the emperor opened the Hall of the Root of Integrity and ordered the crown prince to enter study. Tuo Tuo, the Right Chancellor, and Yabuhua, the Grand Mentor, were placed in charge of the hall's affairs, while Haowen was ordered to serve as Hanlin Academician concurrently as Preceptor of Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: As the crown prince grew older, the emperor opened the Hall of the Root of Integrity and ordered him to study. Right Chancellor Tuo Tuo and Grand Mentor Yabuhua oversaw the hall, while Haowen was named Hanlin academician and preceptor of virtue.

sentences.zh: 好文力辭，上書宰相曰：「三代聖王，莫不以教世子為先務，蓋帝王之治本於道，聖賢之道存於經，而傳經期於明道，出治在於為學，關係至重，要在得人。

translations.literal: Haowen strenuously declined and wrote to the chief minister: "The sage kings of the Three Dynasties all made instructing the heir their foremost task. The root of imperial governance lies in the Way; the Way of sages and worthies resides in the classics; transmitting the classics awaits one who clarifies the Way; bringing forth good government lies in learning—the relation is supremely weighty, and the key lies in obtaining the right man.
translations.idiomatic: Haowen strongly declined and wrote the chief minister: "The sage kings of the Three Dynasties all put instructing the heir first. Imperial governance rests on the Way, the Way of sages rests in the classics, and transmitting the classics requires one who clarifies the Way. Good government depends on learning—the matter is weighty, and the key is finding the right man.

sentences.zh: 自非德堪範模，則不足以輔成德性。

translations.literal: Unless one's virtue suffices to serve as a model, one is not adequate to assist in completing moral character.
translations.idiomatic: Without virtue fit to serve as a model, one cannot help form moral character.

sentences.zh: 自非學臻閫奧，則不足以啟迪聰明。

translations.literal: Unless one's learning reaches the innermost mysteries, one is not adequate to enlighten intelligence.
translations.idiomatic: Without learning that reaches the deepest mysteries, one cannot enlighten the mind.

sentences.zh: 宜求道德之鴻儒，仰成國家之盛事。

translations.literal: One should seek a great Confucian of virtue and learning to accomplish the state's great undertaking.
translations.idiomatic: The state should seek a great Confucian of virtue and learning for this great undertaking.

sentences.zh: 而好文天資本下，人望素輕，草野之習，而久與性成，章句之學，而浸以事廢，驟膺重托，負荷誠難。

translations.literal: Yet Haowen's natural gifts are fundamentally low, public esteem has long been slight, rustic habits have long become his nature, and textual study has gradually been abandoned through affairs—suddenly to bear this heavy trust is truly difficult.
translations.idiomatic: Yet my gifts are modest, my reputation slight, rustic habits are deep in my nature, and textual study has been neglected in official life—to bear this heavy trust suddenly is truly hard.

sentences.zh: 必別加選掄，庶幾國家有得人之助，而好文免妨賢之譏。」

translations.literal: Another selection must be made, so that perhaps the state may gain the help of a worthy man and Haowen may escape the reproach of obstructing the talented."
translations.idiomatic: Another selection should be made so the state may gain a worthy teacher and I may escape the charge of blocking better men."

sentences.zh: 丞相以其書聞，帝嘉嘆之，而不允其辭，好文言：「欲求二帝三王之道，必由於孔氏，其書則《孝經》、《大學》、《論語》、《孟子》、《中庸》。」

translations.literal: The chief minister reported his letter to the emperor, who praised and sighed over it but did not accept his resignation. Haowen said: "To seek the Way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings, one must pass through the House of Kong; the books are the Classic of Filial Piety, the Great Learning, the Analects, Mencius, and the Doctrine of the Mean."
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister reported his letter; the emperor praised it but refused his resignation. Haowen said, "To seek the way of the Two Emperors and Three Kings one must go through Confucius—the books are the Classic of Filial Piety, Great Learning, Analects, Mencius, and Doctrine of the Mean."

sentences.zh: 乃摘其要略，釋以經義，又取史傳及先儒論說，有關治體而協經旨者，加以所見，仿真德秀《大學衍義》之例，為書十一卷，名曰《端本堂經訓要義》，奉表以進，詔付端本堂，令太子習焉。

translations.literal: He then extracted their essentials, explained them with classical meaning, and also took historical writings and earlier Confucian discussions relevant to governance and consonant with the classics, adding his own views. Following the model of Zhen Dexiu's Elaboration on the Great Learning, he made a book in eleven volumes entitled Essential Meanings of the Classics and Instructions for the Hall of the Root of Integrity, submitted it with a memorial, and received an edict assigning it to the hall for the crown prince's study.
translations.idiomatic: He extracted their essentials, explained them by classical meaning, added historical and earlier Confucian passages on governance consonant with the classics, and following Zhen Dexiu's Elaboration on the Great Learning produced eleven volumes entitled Essential Meanings of the Classics and Instructions for the Hall of the Root of Integrity, which he submitted for the crown prince's study.

sentences.zh: 好文又集歷代帝王故事，總百有六篇：一曰聖慧，如漢孝昭、後漢明帝幼敏之類；

translations.literal: Haowen also collected stories of emperors through the ages, 106 pieces in all: first, sage intelligence, such as Emperor Xiaozhao of Han and the youthful keenness of Emperor Ming of Later Han;
translations.idiomatic: Haowen also collected stories of emperors through the ages, 106 in all: first, sage intelligence, such as Emperor Xiaozhao of Han and the youthful keenness of Emperor Ming of Later Han;

sentences.zh: 二曰孝友，如舜、文王及唐玄宗友愛之類；

translations.literal: second, filial piety and brotherly love, such as Shun, King Wen, and the fraternal affection of Emperor Xuanzong of Tang;
translations.idiomatic: second, filial piety and brotherly affection, such as Shun, King Wen, and Emperor Xuanzong of Tang;

sentences.zh: 三曰恭儉，如漢文帝卻千里馬、罷露台之類；

translations.literal: third, respectful frugality, such as Emperor Wen of Han refusing thousand-li horses and abolishing the Terrace for Watching the Battle Array;
translations.idiomatic: third, respectful frugality, such as Emperor Wen of Han refusing thousand-li horses and abolishing the Terrace for Watching the Battle Array;

sentences.zh: 四曰聖學，如殷宗緝學，及陳、隋諸君不善學之類。

translations.literal: fourth, sage learning, such as the Zong of Yin continuing his studies, and the rulers of Chen and Sui who did not study well.
translations.idiomatic: fourth, sage learning, such as the Zong of Yin continuing his studies, and the rulers of Chen and Sui who studied poorly.

sentences.zh: 以為太子問安餘暇之助。

translations.literal: These were intended to aid the crown prince in his leisure after paying respects.
translations.idiomatic: These were meant to aid the crown prince in his leisure after paying respects.

sentences.zh: 又取古史，自三皇迄金、宋，歷代授受，國祚久速，治亂興廢為書，曰《大寶錄》。

translations.literal: He also took ancient histories from the Three Sovereigns through Jin and Song, setting forth successive transmission, the length or brevity of dynastic fortunes, and the rise and fall of order and chaos in a book called Record of the Great Treasure.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled ancient histories from the Three Sovereigns through Jin and Song on dynastic succession, the length of reigns, and the rise and fall of states into Record of the Great Treasure.

sentences.zh: 又取前代帝王是非善惡之所當法當戒者為書，名曰《大寶龜鑑》。

translations.literal: He also compiled what former emperors should emulate or avoid in right and wrong, good and evil, into a book called Tortoise Mirror of the Great Treasure.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled what former emperors should emulate or avoid into Tortoise Mirror of the Great Treasure.

sentences.zh: 皆錄以進焉。

translations.literal: All were recorded and submitted.
translations.idiomatic: All were submitted to the throne.

sentences.zh: 久之，升翰林學士承旨，階榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: After a long while he was promoted to Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts, with the rank of Grand Master for Glorious Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: After a long while he was promoted to Hanlin academician recipient of edicts with the rank of grand master for glorious happiness.

sentences.zh: 十六年，复上書皇太子，其言曰：「臣之所言，即前日所進經典之大意也，殿下宜以所進諸書，參以《貞觀政要》、《大學衍義》等篇，果能一一推而行之，則萬幾之政、太平之治，不難致矣。」

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he again submitted a letter to the crown prince, saying: "What your servant has said is the great purport of the classics submitted the other day. Your Highness should take the books submitted, together with such works as Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign and the Elaboration on the Great Learning—if you can truly carry them out one by one, then the myriad affairs of government and the rule of great peace will not be hard to attain."
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he again wrote the crown prince: "What I have said is the gist of the classics I submitted. Your Highness should study those books together with Essentials of Government from the Zhenguan Reign and Elaboration on the Great Learning—if you truly put them into practice, good government and great peace will not be hard to attain."

sentences.zh: 皇太子深敬禮而嘉納之。

translations.literal: The crown prince deeply respected and gladly accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince deeply respected him and gladly accepted his advice.

sentences.zh: 後屢引年乞致仕，辭至再三，遂拜光祿大夫、河南行省平章政事，仍以翰林學士承旨一品祿終其身。

translations.literal: Later he repeatedly cited his age to request retirement; he declined again and again, and was finally appointed Grand Master for Splendid Happiness and Chief Councillor of the Henan Branch Secretariat, still retaining first-rank salary as Hanlin Academician Recipient of Edicts for life.
translations.idiomatic: Later he repeatedly asked to retire on grounds of age. After repeated refusals he was made grand master for splendid happiness and chief councillor of the Henan branch secretariat, retaining first-rank salary as Hanlin academician recipient of edicts for life.

sentences.zh: ○孛術魯鋋子遠附

translations.literal: ○ Appendix: Borjigidai Chong, courtesy name Ziyuan
translations.idiomatic: Borjigidai Chong (appendix)

sentences.zh: 孛術魯翀，字子翬，其先隆安人。

translations.literal: Borjigidai Chong, courtesy name Zihui, was descended from Long'an.
translations.idiomatic: Borjigidai Chong, whose courtesy name was Zihui, was descended from Long'an.

sentences.zh: 金泰和間，定女直姓氏，屬望廣平。

translations.literal: In the Taihe era of Jin, Jurchen surnames were fixed and they were assigned to Wang of Guangping.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taihe era of Jin, Jurchen surnames were fixed and the clan was assigned to Wang of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 祖德，從憲宗南征，因家鄧之順陽，以功封南陽郡侯。

translations.literal: His grandfather De followed Emperor Xianzong on the southern campaign and settled the family in Shunyang in Deng, enfeoffed as Marquis of Nanyang Commandery for merit.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather De followed Emperor Xianzong south, settled the family in Shunyang in Deng, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Nanyang for merit.

sentences.zh: 父居謙，用翀貴，封南陽郡公。

translations.literal: His father Juqian, through Chong's eminence, was enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery.
translations.idiomatic: His father Juqian, through Chong's eminence, was enfeoffed as duke of Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 初，居謙辟掾江西，以家自隨，生翀贛江舟中，釜鳴者三，人以為異。

translations.literal: Earlier Juqian was recruited as a clerk in Jiangxi and took his family with him. Chong was born on a boat on the Gan River; the cauldron rang three times and people regarded it as strange.
translations.idiomatic: When Juqian was recruited as a clerk in Jiangxi he took his family along. Chong was born on a boat on the Gan River; the cauldron rang three times and people took it as an omen.

sentences.zh: 翀稍長，即勤學。

translations.literal: When Chong grew a little older he studied diligently.
translations.idiomatic: As Chong grew he studied diligently.

sentences.zh: 父歿，家事漸落，翀不恤，而為學益力，乃自順陽復往江西，從新喻蕭克翁學。

translations.literal: When his father died the family fortunes gradually declined. Chong did not care and applied himself all the more to learning; he went from Shunyang back to Jiangxi to study under Xiao Keyong of Xinyu.
translations.idiomatic: After his father died the family fortunes declined. Chong paid no heed and studied all the harder, returning from Shunyang to Jiangxi to study under Xiao Keyong of Xinyu.

sentences.zh: 克翁，宋參政燧之四世孫也，隱居不仕，學行為州里所敬。

translations.literal: Keyong was the fourth-generation descendant of the Song Grand Councilor Sui. He lived in seclusion without taking office; his learning and conduct were respected in the district.
translations.idiomatic: Keyong was the fourth-generation descendant of the Song grand councilor Sui. He lived in seclusion without office, and his learning and conduct were respected locally.

sentences.zh: 嘗夜夢大鳥止其所居，翼覆軒外，舉家驚異，出視之，沖天而去。

translations.literal: Once at night he dreamed a great bird alighted at his dwelling, its wings covering the outer hall. The whole household was startled; going out to look, it soared skyward and departed.
translations.idiomatic: One night he dreamed a great bird alighted at his home, wings covering the outer hall. The household was startled; when they went out to look, it soared away into the sky.

sentences.zh: 明日，翀至。

translations.literal: The next day Chong arrived.
translations.idiomatic: The next day Chong arrived.

sentences.zh: 翀始名思溫，字伯和，克翁為易今名字，以夢故。

translations.literal: Chong at first was named Siwen, courtesy name Bohe; Ke'ong changed them to his present name and courtesy name because of a dream.
translations.idiomatic: Chong had originally been named Siwen, with the courtesy name Bohe; Xiao Keyong changed both to his present name and the courtesy name Zihui, acting on account of a dream.

sentences.zh: 後復從京兆蕭渼遊，其學益宏以肆。

translations.literal: Later he again followed Xiao Mei of Jingzhao in study, and his learning grew ever broader and freer.
translations.idiomatic: He later resumed his studies under Xiao Mei of the capital region, and his scholarship grew ever wider and more assured.

sentences.zh: 翰林學士承旨姚燧以書抵渼曰：「燧見人多矣，學問文章，無足與子翬比倫者。」
