translations.literal: Hanlin Academician Expositor Yao Sui sent a letter to Mei, saying: "Sui has seen many men; in learning and literary composition, none is fit to be ranked with Zihui."
translations.idiomatic: Yao Sui, expositor of the Hanlin Academy, wrote to Xiao Mei: "I have met countless men, yet in scholarship and literary craft I have seen none who can stand comparison with your disciple Zihui."

sentences.zh: 於是渼以女妻之。

translations.literal: Thereupon Mei gave him his daughter in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: On that recommendation Xiao Mei gave him his daughter in marriage.

sentences.zh: 大德十一年，用薦者，授襄陽縣儒學教諭，升汴梁路儒學正。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Dade, on recommendation he was appointed instructor at the Xiangyang County Confucian school and promoted to director of the Bianliang Circuit Confucian school.
translations.idiomatic: In 1307, through recommendation he was appointed Confucian instructor for Xiangyang County and soon promoted to head of the Bianliang circuit Confucian school.

sentences.zh: 會修《世皇實錄》，燧首以翀薦。

translations.literal: When the Veritable Records of the World Emperor were being compiled, Sui was the first to recommend Chong.
translations.idiomatic: When the court undertook the Veritable Records of Kublai, Yao Sui was the first to recommend Chong for the work.

sentences.zh: 至大四年，授翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhida he was appointed compilation officer of the Hanlin National History Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In 1311 he was appointed a compiler in the Hanlin Academy's National History Institute.

sentences.zh: 延祐二年，擢河東道廉訪司經歷，遷陝西行台監察御史，賑濟吐蕃，多所建白。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yanyou he was promoted to secretary of the Hedong Surveillance Commission, then transferred to investigating censor on the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, relieving distress in Tibet; he submitted many proposals.
translations.idiomatic: In 1315 he was promoted to secretary of the Hedong surveillance office, then made investigating censor on the Shaanxi branch secretariat, where he oversaw famine relief in Tibet and submitted numerous memorials.

sentences.zh: 五年，拜監察御史。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he was appointed investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: In 1318 he was appointed investigating censor at court.

sentences.zh: 時英皇未出閣，翀言：「宜擇正人以輔導。」

translations.literal: At that time the Heir Apparent had not yet left the palace school; Chong said: "One should choose upright men to instruct and guide him."
translations.idiomatic: The heir apparent had not yet been installed in his own residence; Chong urged that upright tutors be chosen to guide him.

sentences.zh: 帝嘉納之。

translations.literal: The emperor praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor commended the advice and adopted it.

sentences.zh: 尋劾奏中書參議元明善，帝初怒，不納，明日，乃命改明善他官，而傳旨慰諭翀。

translations.literal: Soon afterward he memorialized impeaching Zhongshu Secretariat participant Yuan Mingshan; at first the emperor was angry and did not accept it, but the next day he ordered Mingshan transferred to another post and sent an edict comforting Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He soon impeached Yuan Mingshan, a participant in the Secretariat; the emperor at first refused the charge in anger, yet the next day reassigned Mingshan and sent Chong a message of reassurance.

sentences.zh: 巡按遼陽，有旨給以弓矢環刀。

translations.literal: On inspection tour in Liaoyang, an edict granted him bow, arrows, and ring-handled saber.
translations.idiomatic: While on inspection in Liaoyang he received an imperial order granting him bow, arrows, and the ring-handled saber borne by touring censors.

sentences.zh: 後因為定制。

translations.literal: Later this therefore became a fixed regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The grant was later codified as standard practice.

sentences.zh: 還往淮東核憲司官聲跡，淮東憲臣，惟尚刑，多置獄具，翀曰：「國家所以立風紀，蓋將肅清天下，初不尚刑也。」

translations.literal: Returning, he went to Huaidong to review surveillance officials' reputations and conduct; the Huaidong surveillance commissioners valued punishment alone and set out many instruments of torture; Chong said: "The reason the state establishes discipline is to bring the realm under clear order; it does not at the outset value punishment."
translations.idiomatic: On his return he was sent to Huaidong to audit the conduct of surveillance commissioners, who there prized punishment above all and kept extensive torture gear on hand. Chong told them, "The state establishes discipline to purify the realm, not to make cruelty its first principle."

sentences.zh: 取其獄具焚之。

translations.literal: He took their instruments of torture and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He seized those implements and had them burned.

sentences.zh: 時有旨凡以吏進者，例降二等，從七品以上不得用。

translations.literal: At that time an edict decreed that all who had advanced through clerical service should, as a rule, be demoted two ranks, and none above the seventh sub-rank might be employed.
translations.idiomatic: An edict then required that officials who had risen through clerical ranks be demoted two grades by rule, and that none above the seventh sub-rank be appointed.

sentences.zh: 翀言：「科舉未立，人才多以吏進，若一概屈抑，恐未足盡天下持平之議。

translations.literal: Chong said: "The civil-service examinations are not yet established; talent mostly advances through clerical service; if one uniformly suppresses them, I fear that may not fully satisfy the realm's sense of fair balance.
translations.idiomatic: Chong argued, "With the examination system still unsettled, most talent still enters through clerical service; to suppress such men wholesale would hardly satisfy fair opinion across the empire.

sentences.zh: 請吏進者，宜止於五品。」

translations.literal: I ask that those advancing through clerical service should be limited to the fifth rank."
translations.idiomatic: He proposed that clerical appointees be capped at the fifth rank."

sentences.zh: 許之，因著為令。

translations.literal: It was granted, and thereby written into regulation.
translations.idiomatic: The court agreed and inscribed the rule in law.

sentences.zh: 除右司都事。

translations.literal: He was appointed associate director of the Right Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed associate director of the Right Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 時相鐵木迭兒專事刑戮，以復私憾，翀因避去。

translations.literal: At that time the chief minister Temuder devoted himself to executions and punishments to settle private grudges; Chong therefore withdrew to avoid him.
translations.idiomatic: The chief minister Temuder was then bent on executions to settle private scores, and Chong withdrew to keep clear of him.

sentences.zh: 頃之，擢翰林修撰，又改左司都事。

translations.literal: Before long he was promoted to Hanlin compiler, then again made associate director of the Left Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Shortly afterward he was promoted to Hanlin compiler, then transferred back to associate director of the Left Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 於是拜住為左相，使人勞翀曰：「今規模已定，不同往日，宜早至也。」

translations.literal: Thereupon Bainu became left chancellor and sent someone to console Chong, saying: "The framework is now settled and unlike former days; you should come early."
translations.idiomatic: Bainu then became left chancellor and sent a messenger to urge Chong: "The new order is fixed and unlike the old days—you should return without delay."

sentences.zh: 翀強為起。

translations.literal: Chong forced himself to rise and go.
translations.idiomatic: Chong reluctantly accepted and took up his post.

sentences.zh: 會國子監隸中書，俾翀兼領之。

translations.literal: As the Directorate of the National University had come under the Secretariat, Chong was ordered to head it concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: When the National University was placed under the Secretariat, Chong was assigned to direct it as well.

sentences.zh: 先是，陝西有變，府縣之官多罣罥者，翀白丞相曰：「此輩皆脅從，非同情者。」

translations.literal: Earlier there had been unrest in Shaanxi, and many prefectural and county officials were entangled in it; Chong told the chancellor: "These people were all coerced into following; they were not of one mind with the rebels."
translations.idiomatic: After the Shaanxi uprising many local officials had been implicated; Chong told the chancellor, "They followed under duress and did not share the rebels' aims."

sentences.zh: 乃悉加銓敘。

translations.literal: Thereupon they were all reappointed through review.
translations.idiomatic: They were all reinstated through review.

sentences.zh: 帝方獵柳林，駐故東平王安童碑所，因獻《駐蹕頌》，皆稱旨，命坐，賜飲尚尊。

translations.literal: The emperor was then hunting at Willow Grove and halted at the site of the former stele of Dongping Prince An Tong; Chong presented an "Ode to the Imperial Halting," all of which pleased the emperor, who ordered him seated and granted him drink from the imperial goblet.
translations.idiomatic: While the emperor hunted at Willow Grove he paused at the stele of the former Prince of Dongping, An Tong; Chong presented an "Ode to the Imperial Halting," won high praise, was bidden to sit, and was served wine from the imperial cup.

sentences.zh: 從幸上京，次龍虎台，拜住命翀傳​​旨中書，翀領之，行數步，還曰：「命翀傳否？」

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial progress to Shangdu, they stopped at Longhutai; Bainu ordered Chong to relay an edict to the Secretariat; Chong acknowledged it, walked several paces, then returned and said: "Was I ordered to relay it, or not?"
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to Shangdu the party halted at Longhutai; Bainu told Chong to convey an edict to the Secretariat. Chong acknowledged the order, walked a few steps, then turned back and asked, "Am I indeed to convey this edict?"

sentences.zh: 拜住歎曰：「真謹飭人也。」

translations.literal: Bainu sighed and said: "Truly a man of strict propriety."
translations.idiomatic: Bainu sighed and said, "What a scrupulous man."

sentences.zh: 間謂翀曰：「爾可作宰相否？」

translations.literal: In passing he asked Chong: "Could you serve as chancellor?"
translations.idiomatic: He then asked Chong in private, "Could you serve as chancellor?"

sentences.zh: 翀對曰：「宰相固不敢當，然所學，宰相事也。

translations.literal: Chong replied: "I certainly dare not presume to the chancellorship, yet what I have studied is the work of a chancellor.
translations.idiomatic: Chong answered, "I would not presume to claim the post, yet what I have studied is precisely the chancellor's craft.

sentences.zh: 夫為宰相者，必福德才量四者皆備，乃足當耳。」

translations.literal: One who would be chancellor must have all four—virtue, good fortune, talent, and breadth of capacity—only then is he fit for it."
translations.idiomatic: A true chancellor must unite virtue, fortune, talent, and breadth of capacity—only when all four are present is the office truly filled."

sentences.zh: 拜住大悅，以酒觴翀曰：「非公，不聞此言。」

translations.literal: Bainu was greatly pleased and raised his cup to Chong, saying: "Had it not been for you, I would not have heard these words."
translations.idiomatic: Bainu was delighted, raised his cup to Chong, and said, "But for you I would never have heard such words."

sentences.zh: 迎駕至行在所，翀入見，帝賜之坐。

translations.literal: Meeting the imperial carriage at the traveling palace, Chong entered audience and the emperor granted him a seat.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor arrived at the traveling palace Chong was received in audience and granted a seat.

sentences.zh: 升右司員外郎，奉旨預修《大元通制》，書成，翀為之序。

translations.literal: He was promoted to vice director of the Right Secretariat and, by imperial order, took part in compiling the Comprehensive Statutes of the Great Yuan; when the book was finished, Chong wrote its preface.
translations.idiomatic: Promoted to vice director of the Right Secretariat, he helped compile the Comprehensive Statutes of the Great Yuan by imperial commission and wrote the preface when the work was complete.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，遷國子司業。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding he was transferred to vice director of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: In 1324 he was made vice director of the National University.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為河南行省左右司郎中。

translations.literal: The next year he went out as director of the Left and Right Secretariats of the Henan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was posted as director of the Henan branch secretariat's left and right bureaus.

sentences.zh: 丞相曰：「吾得賢佐矣。」

translations.literal: The chancellor said: "I have gained a worthy assistant."
translations.idiomatic: The provincial chancellor said, "I have gained a worthy assistant at last."

sentences.zh: 翀曰：「世祖立國，成憲具在，慎守足矣。

translations.literal: Chong said: "Shizu founded the state; the completed statutes are all in place—careful preservation is enough.
translations.idiomatic: Chong replied, "Kublai founded the dynasty and left its institutions complete; our task is careful stewardship, nothing more.

sentences.zh: 譬若乘舟，非一人之力所能運也。」

translations.literal: It is like riding in a boat: not one man's strength alone can move it."
translations.idiomatic: It is like steering a great vessel—no single hand can move it alone."

sentences.zh: 翀乃開壅除弊，省務為之一新。

translations.literal: Chong then cleared blockages and removed abuses, and provincial affairs were made wholly new.
translations.idiomatic: Chong cleared obstructions and swept away abuses until provincial administration was wholly renewed.

sentences.zh: 三年，擢燕南河北道廉訪使，晉州達魯花赤有罪就逮，而奉使宣撫以印帖征之，欲緩其事，翀發其奸，奉使因遁去。

translations.literal: In the third year he was promoted to surveillance commissioner of the Yannan and Hebei Circuit; the darughachi of Jin Prefecture, guilty, was taken into custody, but a commissioner on pacification mission used his seal warrant to summon him, wishing to delay the matter; Chong exposed the fraud, and the commissioner therefore fled.
translations.idiomatic: In 1326 he was made surveillance commissioner for Yannan and Hebei. When a guilty darughachi of Jinzhou was arrested, a pacification commissioner tried to summon him away with a sealed warrant to stall the case; Chong exposed the scheme and the commissioner fled.

sentences.zh: 入僉太常禮儀院事，盜竊太廟神主，翀言：「各室宜增設都監員，內外嚴置局鎖，晝巡夜警，永為定制。」

translations.literal: He entered the court as associate director of the Directorate of Imperial Rites; when spirit tablets in the Imperial Ancestral Temple were stolen, Chong said: "Each chamber should have added chief overseers; inside and outside, locks and wards should be set strictly; day patrol and night watch should be made a permanent regulation."
translations.idiomatic: Appointed associate director of the Directorate of Imperial Rites, he responded to the theft of ancestral spirit tablets by proposing additional chief wardens for each shrine chamber, strict inner and outer locks, and permanent day-and-night patrols.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: It was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The court adopted his plan.

sentences.zh: 又纂修《太常集禮》，書成而未上，有旨命翀兼經筵官。

translations.literal: He also compiled the Collected Rites of the Imperial Rites Directorate; when the book was finished it had not yet been submitted, when an edict ordered Chong to serve concurrently as lecturer at the Classics Colloquium.
translations.idiomatic: He also compiled the Collected Rites of the Directorate of Imperial Rites; before the finished work could be submitted, an edict named him a lecturer at the Classics Colloquium as well.

sentences.zh: 文宗之入也，大臣問以典故，翀所建白近漢文故事，眾皆是之。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong entered the capital, the great ministers inquired about precedents; the proposals Chong submitted closely followed the precedents of Emperor Wen of Han, and all approved them.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong entered the capital the ministers asked about ceremonial precedent; Chong's proposals, modeled on the accession of Emperor Wen of Han, won universal assent.

sentences.zh: 文宗嘗字呼子翬而不名。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong would at times call him by his courtesy name Zihui and not by his personal name.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong sometimes addressed him by his courtesy name Zihui rather than by his personal name—a mark of exceptional favor.

sentences.zh: 命翀與平章政事溫迪罕等十人，商論大事，日夕備顧問，宿直東廡下。

translations.literal: He ordered Chong, together with Grand Councillor Undihen and nine others—ten men in all—to deliberate on great affairs, ready as advisers from morning to night, lodging on duty beneath the eastern wing.
translations.idiomatic: He appointed Chong, Grand Councillor Undihen, and eight others—ten men in all—to deliberate on state affairs, keeping them at hand day and night as counselors quartered in the eastern wing.

sentences.zh: 文宗虛大位以俟明宗，翀極言：「大兄遠在朔漠，北兵有阻，神器不可久虛，宜攝位以俟其至。」

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong left the great throne vacant to await Emperor Mingzong; Chong spoke urgently: "The elder brother is far off in the northern deserts, and northern troops obstruct the way; the sacred vessel cannot long stand empty—he should assume the regency until Mingzong arrives."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong left the throne vacant awaiting Emperor Mingzong; Chong urged strongly, "Your elder brother is far in the northern steppe and the northern armies block the road—the throne cannot stand empty. You should rule as regent until he arrives."

sentences.zh: 文宗納其言。

translations.literal: Emperor Wenzong accepted his words.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wenzong took his counsel.

sentences.zh: 及文宗親祀天地、社稷、宗廟，翀為禮儀使，詳記行禮節文於笏，遇至尊不敢直書，必識以兩圈，帝偶取笏視，曰：「此為皇帝字乎？」

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong personally sacrificed to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temple, Chong served as ritual commissioner, recording the ritual stages in detail on his tablet; encountering the supreme title he dared not write it directly and always marked it with two circles; the emperor once took the tablet to look and said: "Is this the character for 'emperor'?"
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wenzong personally offered sacrifice to Heaven and Earth, the altars of soil and grain, and the ancestral temple, Chong served as ritual commissioner and noted each ceremonial step on his court tablet; wherever the imperial title appeared he marked it with two circles rather than write it outright. The emperor once glanced at the tablet and asked, "Is that meant for the word 'emperor'?"

sentences.zh: 因大笑，以笏還翀。

translations.literal: He thereupon laughed greatly and returned the tablet to Chong.
translations.idiomatic: He laughed aloud and returned the tablet to Chong.

sentences.zh: 竣事，上《天歷大慶詩》三章，帝命藏之奎章閣。

translations.literal: When the rites were concluded, he submitted three chapters of "Great Celebration Poems of the Tianli Reign"; the emperor ordered them stored in the Kuizhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: After the rites he presented three "Great Celebration Poems of the Tianli Reign"; the emperor ordered them stored in the Kuizhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 擢陝西漢中道廉訪使。

translations.literal: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner of the Shaanxi and Hanzhong Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to surveillance commissioner for Shaanxi and Hanzhong.

sentences.zh: 會立太禧院，除僉太禧宗禋院，兼祗承神御殿事，詔遣使趣之還。

translations.literal: When the Grand Felicity Directorate was established, he was appointed associate director of its Ancestral Sacrifice Institute and concurrently charged with maintaining the Spirit-Veneration Hall; an edict sent envoys to urge his return.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Felicity Directorate was established he was made its associate director for ancestral sacrifice and put in charge of the Spirit-Veneration Hall; the court sent envoys to hurry his return.

sentences.zh: 迎駕至龍虎台，帝問：「子翬來何緩？」

translations.literal: Meeting the imperial carriage at Longhutai, the emperor asked: "Why has Zihui come so slowly?"
translations.idiomatic: Meeting the emperor at Longhutai, the emperor asked, "Why has Zihui been so long in coming?"

sentences.zh: 太禧院使阿榮對曰：「翀體豐肥，不任乘馬，從水道來，是以緩耳。」

translations.literal: The director of the Grand Felicity Directorate, Arong, replied: "Chong's body is full and stout; he cannot bear riding horseback and came by water route—hence the delay."
translations.idiomatic: Arong, director of the Grand Felicity Directorate, answered, "Chong is stout of build and cannot endure horseback travel; he came by water, and that is why he is late."

sentences.zh: 太禧臣日聚禁中，以便顧問，帝嘗問阿榮曰：「魯子翬飲食何如？」

translations.literal: The Grand Felicity officials gathered daily within the Forbidden City for ready consultation; the emperor once asked Arong: "How is Lu Zihui's food and drink?"
translations.idiomatic: Grand Felicity officials gathered daily in the palace for consultation; the emperor once asked Arong, "How does Lu Zihui fare at table?"

sentences.zh: 對曰：「與眾人同。」

translations.literal: He replied: "The same as everyone else's."
translations.idiomatic: He answered that Chong ate no differently from the others.

sentences.zh: 又問：「談論如何？」

translations.literal: He asked again: "How is his discourse?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "What of his conversation?"

sentences.zh: 曰：「翀所談，義理之言也。」

translations.literal: He said: "What Chong discusses are words of principle and reason."
translations.idiomatic: Arong said, "Chong speaks only in the language of moral principle."

sentences.zh: 從幸上都，嘗奉敕撰碑文，稱旨，帝曰：「候朕還大都，當還汝潤筆貲也。」

translations.literal: Accompanying the imperial progress to Shangdu, he once received an edict to compose a stele inscription; it pleased the emperor, who said: "When I return to Dadu I shall repay your brush-and-ink fee."
translations.idiomatic: On the journey to Shangdu he composed a stele inscription by imperial order to great acclaim; the emperor said, "When I return to Dadu I shall pay your writer's fee."

sentences.zh: 遷集賢直學士，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to academician-expositor of the Jixian Hall and concurrently made chancellor of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: He was made academician-expositor of the Jixian Hall and concurrently chancellor of the National University.

sentences.zh: 諸生素已望翀，至是，私相歡賀。

translations.literal: The students had long looked up to Chong; at this they privately rejoiced together.
translations.idiomatic: The students had long revered him; now they celebrated among themselves.

sentences.zh: 翀以古者教育有業，退必有居。

translations.literal: Chong held that in antiquity education had its profession, and on leaving study one necessarily had a dwelling.
translations.idiomatic: Chong held that in antiquity learning was a calling and that students, on leaving school, must have somewhere to live.

sentences.zh: 舊制，弟子員初入學，以羊贄，所貳之品與羊等。

translations.literal: Under the old regulation, when student members first entered study they presented sheep as tribute gifts, and the secondary goods presented matched the sheep in value.
translations.idiomatic: By old custom new students presented sheep as entrance gifts, with secondary offerings matched to the sheep's value.

sentences.zh: 翀曰：「與其饜口腹，孰若為吾黨燥濕寒暑之虞乎！」

translations.literal: Chong said: "Rather than fill bellies, would it not be better to spare our fellows worry over dry and wet, cold and heat!"
translations.idiomatic: Chong said, "Better to shelter our fellows from heat and cold than to fill a few stomachs for a day."

sentences.zh: 命撙集之，得錢二萬緡有奇，作屋四區，以居學者。

translations.literal: He ordered the gifts collected and economized, obtaining a little more than twenty thousand strings of cash, and built four compounds to house the students.
translations.idiomatic: He had the gifts pooled instead, raising more than twenty thousand strings of cash, and built four dormitory compounds for the students.

sentences.zh: 諸生積分，有六年未及釋褐者，翀至，皆使就試而官之。

translations.literal: Students accumulating credits—some six years without yet being released from student status to take office—when Chong arrived, he had them all sit for examination and be appointed.
translations.idiomatic: Some students had accumulated six years of credit without yet qualifying for office; Chong had them all examined and appointed.

sentences.zh: 帝師至京師，有旨朝臣一品以下，皆乘白馬郊迎。

translations.literal: When the Imperial Preceptor reached the capital, an edict decreed that court officials of the first rank and below should all ride white horses to greet him in the suburbs.
translations.idiomatic: When the Imperial Preceptor reached the capital, an edict required officials of the first rank and below to ride white horses and meet him in the suburbs.

sentences.zh: 大臣俯伏進觴，帝師不為動，惟翀舉觴立進曰：「帝師，釋迦之徒，天下僧人師也。

translations.literal: The great ministers prostrated themselves and advanced the cup; the Imperial Preceptor did not stir—only Chong raised the cup and, standing, advanced it, saying: "Imperial Preceptor, you are of Shakyamuni's lineage, teacher of all monks under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: The ministers prostrated themselves and offered the cup, but the Imperial Preceptor did not respond—only Chong stood forward with the cup and said, "Imperial Preceptor, you are of Shakyamuni's line, teacher to all monks under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 餘，孔子之徒，天下儒人師也。

translations.literal: As for the rest of us, we are of Confucius's lineage, teachers of all scholars under Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: As for the rest of us, we are disciples of Confucius, teachers to all scholars under Heaven.

sentences.zh: 請各不為禮。」

translations.literal: I ask that each of us forgo such obeisance."
translations.idiomatic: Let us each dispense with such obeisance."

sentences.zh: 帝師笑而起，舉觴卒飲，眾為之栗然。

translations.literal: The Imperial Preceptor smiled, rose, raised the cup, and finished the drink; the assembly was awestruck on his account.
translations.idiomatic: The Imperial Preceptor smiled, rose, drained the cup, and the whole assembly stood in awe.

sentences.zh: 文宗崩，皇太后聽政，命別不花、塔失海牙、阿兒思蘭、馬祖常、史顯夫及翀六人，商論國政。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wenzong died, the empress dowager held court and ordered Biebuqa, Tashihaiya, Arsalan, Ma Zuchang, Shi Xianfu, and Chong—six men—to deliberate on state affairs.
translations.idiomatic: After Emperor Wenzong's death the empress dowager ruled as regent and appointed Biebuqa, Tashihaiya, Arsalan, Ma Zuchang, Shi Xianfu, and Chong—six men—to deliberate on state affairs.

sentences.zh: 翀以大位不可久虛，請嗣君即位，早正宸極，以幸天下。

translations.literal: Chong held that the great throne could not long stand empty and asked that the heir ascend promptly, establishing the imperial seat early to bring fortune to the realm.
translations.idiomatic: Chong urged that the throne could not remain vacant and that the heir should ascend at once to steady the realm.

sentences.zh: 帝既即位，大臣以為赦不可頻行，翀曰：「今上以聖子神孫，入繼大統，當新天下耳目。

translations.literal: After the emperor had ascended, the great ministers held that amnesties should not be issued frequently; Chong said: "Now that His Majesty, a sage son and divine grandson, has entered to succeed the great succession, he should renew the ears and eyes of the realm.
translations.idiomatic: After the new emperor's accession the ministers argued against frequent amnesties; Chong said, "His Majesty has entered the succession as a sage son and divine grandson—the realm's eyes and ears must be renewed.

sentences.zh: 今不赦，豈可收怨於新造之君乎！」

translations.literal: If there is no amnesty now, how can one avoid gathering resentment against a newly established sovereign!"
translations.idiomatic: Without an amnesty now, how can we avoid heaping resentment on a newly enthroned sovereign?"

sentences.zh: 皇太后以為宜從翀言，議乃定。

translations.literal: The empress dowager held that Chong's words should be followed, and the deliberation was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The empress dowager sided with Chong, and the matter was settled.

sentences.zh: 遷禮部尚書，階中憲大夫。

translations.literal: He was transferred to minister of the Ministry of Rites, with the rank of Central Rectitude Grandee.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to minister of rites with the rank of Central Rectitude Grandee.

sentences.zh: 有大官妻無子而妾有子者，其妻以田盡入於僧寺，其子訟之，翀召其妻詰之曰：「汝為人妻，不以資產遺其子，他日何面目見汝夫於地下！」

translations.literal: There was a case of a great officer's wife who had no son while a concubine had a son; the wife gave all the fields into a Buddhist monastery; the son sued; Chong summoned the wife and questioned her, saying: "You are a man's wife—why do you not leave your property to your son? What face will you have one day to meet your husband beneath the earth!"
translations.idiomatic: A senior official's wife, childless while a concubine had borne a son, had given all the family land to a monastery; the son sued, and Chong summoned the wife and rebuked her: "As a wife you withhold your property from your son—what face will you show your husband in the grave!"

sentences.zh: 卒反其田。

translations.literal: In the end the fields were returned.
translations.idiomatic: The land was restored to the son.

sentences.zh: 元統二年，除江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yuantong he was appointed vice administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In 1334 he was appointed vice administrator of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 逾年，以遷葬故歸鄉里。

translations.literal: After more than a year, on account of relocating a burial he returned to his home district.
translations.idiomatic: A year later he returned home to oversee a family reburial.

sentences.zh: 明年，召為翰林侍講學士，以疾辭，不上。

translations.literal: The next year he was summoned as Hanlin exposition academician but declined on grounds of illness and did not go up.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was summoned as Hanlin exposition academician but declined on grounds of illness and never returned to court.

sentences.zh: 至元四年卒，年六十。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he died, aged sixty.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he died at the age of sixty.

sentences.zh: 贈通奉大夫、陝西行省參知政事、護軍，追封南陽郡公，諡文靖。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, vice administrator of the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, and protector of the army; posthumously enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang Commandery, with the posthumous title Wenjing.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously honored as Grand Master for Splendid Happiness, vice administrator of the Shaanxi branch secretariat, and protector of the army; enfeoffed as Duke of Nanyang with the posthumous title Wenjing.

sentences.zh: 翀狀貌魁梧，不妄言笑。

translations.literal: Chong's stature was imposing and tall; he did not speak or laugh lightly.
translations.idiomatic: Chong was tall and imposing, grave in speech and seldom given to laughter.

sentences.zh: 其為學一本於性命道德，而記問宏博，異言僻語，無不淹貫。

translations.literal: His learning took nature, fate, and moral principle as its root, yet his erudition and recall were vast; strange words and recondite expressions—none escaped his thorough mastery.
translations.idiomatic: His scholarship rooted in the moral nature of the self, yet his erudition was vast and no recondite text or strange doctrine lay beyond his grasp.

sentences.zh: 文章簡奧典雅，深合古法。

translations.literal: His writings were concise, profound, elegant, and classical, deeply conforming to ancient methods.
translations.idiomatic: His prose was concise, profound, and classically elegant, in full accord with ancient models.

sentences.zh: 用是天下學者，仰為表儀。

translations.literal: Because of this, scholars throughout the realm looked up to him as a model.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars across the empire looked to him as their standard.

sentences.zh: 其居國學者久，論者謂自許衡之後，能以師道自任者，惟耶律有尚及翀而已。

translations.literal: He dwelt long at the National University; commentators said that after Xu Heng, only Yelü Youshang and Chong could take the teacher's way upon themselves.
translations.idiomatic: He served long at the National University; later opinion held that after Xu Heng, only Yelü Youshang and Chong truly bore the teacher's mantle.

sentences.zh: 有文集六十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in sixty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to sixty juan.

sentences.zh: 子遠，字朋道，以翀廕調秘書郎，轉襄陽縣尹，須次居南陽。

translations.literal: His son Yuan, courtesy name Pengdao, through Chong's hereditary privilege was appointed secretary; he was transferred to magistrate of Xiangyang County and, awaiting his turn in office, resided in Nanyang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuan, courtesy name Pengdao, entered office through Chong's yin privilege as a secretary, then became magistrate of Xiangyang and, while awaiting appointment, lived in Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 賊起，遠以忠義自奮，傾財募丁壯，得千餘人，與賊拒戰，俄而賊大至，遠被害死。

translations.literal: When bandits rose, Yuan roused himself through loyalty and righteousness, poured out his wealth to recruit able-bodied men, obtained more than a thousand, and fought the bandits in resistance; soon the bandits came in great force and Yuan was killed.
translations.idiomatic: When rebels rose Yuan rallied to the defense, spent his fortune to raise more than a thousand men, and fought the rebels until a larger force arrived and killed him.

sentences.zh: 遠妻雷為賊所執，賊欲妻之，乃詆賊曰：「我魯參政塚婦，縣令嫡妻，夫死不貳，肯從汝狗彘以生乎！」

translations.literal: Yuan's wife Lei was seized by bandits; the bandits wished to take her as wife; she reviled them, saying: "I am the daughter-in-law at the tomb of Counselor Lu, the magistrate's lawful wife—my husband is dead and I will not be unfaithful; would I consent to live following you dogs and swine!"
translations.idiomatic: Yuan's wife Lei was captured; the rebels wished to take her, but she reviled them: "I am the widow of Counselor Lu's house and a magistrate's lawful wife—my husband is dead and I am faithful; would I live as the mate of dogs and swine like you!"

sentences.zh: 賊醜其言，將辱之，雷號哭大罵，不從，乃見殺。

translations.literal: The bandits were shamed by her words and were about to violate her; Lei wailed and cursed loudly, would not submit, and was therefore killed.
translations.idiomatic: Enraged by her words, they moved to violate her; Lei wailed and cursed them until they killed her.

sentences.zh: 舉家皆被害。

translations.literal: The whole household perished.
translations.idiomatic: The entire household was slain.

sentences.zh: ○李枿

translations.literal: ○ Li Jiong
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiong

sentences.zh: 李泂，字溉之，滕州人。

translations.literal: Li Jiong, courtesy name Guaizhi, was a native of Tengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Jiong, whose courtesy name was Guaizhi, came from Tengzhou.

sentences.zh: 生有異質，始從學，即穎悟強記。

translations.literal: From birth he had extraordinary gifts; as soon as he began study, he was sharp-witted and possessed a powerful memory.
translations.idiomatic: He was gifted from birth, and from his first days of study he proved exceptionally quick and retentive.

sentences.zh: 作為文辭，如宿習者。

translations.literal: When he composed literary writings, it was as though he had long practiced.
translations.idiomatic: When he wrote, it seemed the work of long practice.

sentences.zh: 姚燧以文章負大名，一見其文，深嘆異之，力荐於朝，授翰林國史院編修官。

translations.literal: Yao Sui enjoyed great fame for his literary compositions; upon seeing Jiong's writings once, he deeply marveled and exclaimed in admiration, strongly recommended him at court, and he was appointed Compiler at the Hanlin Academy National History Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yao Sui was renowned for his writing. After a single reading of Jiong's work he was deeply impressed and pressed his case at court; Jiong was appointed a compiler at the Hanlin Academy National History Office.

sentences.zh: 未幾，以親老，就養江南。

translations.literal: Before long, because his parents were aged, he went to support them in the Jiangnan region.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward, with elderly parents to care for, he went south to support them in Jiangnan.

sentences.zh: 久之，辟中書掾，非其志也。

translations.literal: After a long time, he was summoned as a Secretariat clerk, which was not his wish.
translations.idiomatic: After some years he was recruited as a clerk in the Secretariat, a post that did not suit his inclinations.

sentences.zh: 及考除集賢院都事，轉太常博士。

translations.literal: When he passed the examination and was cleared for appointment as Supervisor of Affairs at the Academy of Gathered Worthies, he was transferred to Doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.
translations.idiomatic: He passed the examination and was appointed supervisor of affairs at the Academy of Gathered Worthies, then was transferred to doctor of the Imperial Ancestral Temple.

sentences.zh: 拜住為丞相，聞泂名，擢監修國史長史，歷秘書監著作郎、太常禮儀院經歷。

translations.literal: When Bayan served as chief councillor, hearing Jiong's reputation, he promoted him to Chief Administrator for the Supervision of the National History, and he successively served as Compiler at the Directorate of Books and Manager at the Imperial Ancestral Temple Rites Institute.
translations.idiomatic: When Bayan became chief councillor he heard of Jiong's reputation and promoted him to chief administrator for supervising the national history; he later served as compiler at the Directorate of Books and manager at the Imperial Ancestral Temple Rites Institute.

sentences.zh: 泰定初，除翰林待制，以親喪未克葬，辭而歸。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taiding, he was appointed Hanlin Attending Draftsman; because his parent's mourning had not yet been interred, he declined and returned home.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Taiding reign he was made a Hanlin attending draftsman, but with a parent still unburied in mourning he declined the post and went home.

sentences.zh: 天歷初，復以待制召。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianli, he was again summoned as Attending Draftsman.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Tianli reign he was recalled as an attending draftsman.

sentences.zh: 於是文宗方開奎章閣，延天下知名士充學士員，泂數進見，奏對稱旨，超遷翰林直學士，俄特授奎章閣承製學士。

translations.literal: At that time Emperor Wenzong had just opened the Kui Zhang Pavilion, inviting renowned men throughout the realm to fill positions as academicians; Jiong repeatedly had audience, and in memorial responses pleased the intent; he was specially promoted to Hanlin Direct Academician, and soon was specially appointed Kui Zhang Pavilion Bachelor for Drafting.
translations.idiomatic: The Emperor Wenzong had just opened the Kui Zhang Pavilion and gathered famous scholars from across the empire as its academicians. Jiong appeared before him often; his replies in audience pleased the throne, and he was quickly promoted to Hanlin direct academician, then specially appointed a drafting academician at the Kui Zhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 泂既為帝所知遇，乃著書曰《輔治篇》以進，文宗嘉納之。

translations.literal: Since Jiong had already won the emperor's knowledge and favor, he then wrote a book called Chapters on Assisting Governance and presented it; Emperor Wenzong praised and accepted it.
translations.idiomatic: Once the emperor knew and favored him, Jiong composed the Chapters on Assisting Governance and presented it; Wenzong received it with approval.

sentences.zh: 朝廷有大議，必使與焉。

translations.literal: When the court had great deliberations, he was invariably made to participate.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the court took up a major question, he was always included.

sentences.zh: 會詔修《經世大典》，泂方臥疾，即強起，曰：「此大製作也，吾其可以不預！」

translations.literal: It happened that an edict ordered the compilation of the Great Compendium for Governing the Age; Jiong was just lying ill, yet immediately forced himself to rise, saying: "This is a great production—how can I not take part!"
translations.idiomatic: When an edict went out to compile the Great Compendium for Governing the Age, Jiong was bedridden, yet he roused himself at once and said, "This is a work of the first rank—how could I stay out of it!"

sentences.zh: 力疾同修。

translations.literal: He strained against illness to compile it jointly.
translations.idiomatic: He forced himself from his sickbed to join the editors.

sentences.zh: 書成，既進奏，旋謁告以歸。

translations.literal: When the book was completed and he had presented it at audience, he straightway requested leave and returned.
translations.idiomatic: When the work was finished and presented, he promptly asked leave and went home.

sentences.zh: 复除翰林直學士，遣使召之，竟以疾不能起。

translations.literal: He was again appointed Hanlin Direct Academician; envoys were sent to summon him, but in the end due to illness he could not rise.
translations.idiomatic: He was again made Hanlin direct academician and messengers were sent to fetch him, but in the end his illness left him unable to rise.

sentences.zh: 泂骨骼清峻，神情開朗，秀眉疏髯，目瑩如電，顏面如冰玉，而脣如渥丹然，峨冠褒衣，望之者疑為神仙中人也。

translations.literal: Jiong's frame was clear and lofty, his spirit bright and open; he had fine brows and a sparse beard, eyes gleaming like lightning, a face like ice and jade, and lips like lustrous cinnabar; wearing a high cap and full robes, those who looked upon him suspected he was a man among immortals.
translations.idiomatic: Jiong had a spare, elegant frame and an open, luminous bearing: fine brows, a light beard, eyes bright as lightning, a face like polished jade, lips the color of cinnabar. In his high cap and flowing robes he seemed to onlookers a figure from the realm of immortals.

sentences.zh: 其為文章，奮筆揮灑，迅飛疾動，汩汩滔滔，思態疊出，縱橫奇變，若紛錯而有條理，意之所至，臻極神妙。

translations.literal: When he composed literary works, he wielded the brush with sweeping vigor, swift as flight and quick in motion, pouring forth in an unbroken torrent; modes of thought layered upon one another, ranging freely in marvelous transformations—as though tangled yet with inner order; wherever his intent reached, he attained the utmost of divine subtlety.
translations.idiomatic: In his writing he swept the brush with abandon—swift, torrential, thought upon thought unfolding in startling turns that seemed chaotic yet held their own order. Whatever he aimed at, he carried to a kind of inspired perfection.

sentences.zh: 泂每以李太白自似，當世亦以是許之。

translations.literal: Jiong often likened himself to Li Taibai, and his contemporaries granted him that as well.
translations.idiomatic: He often compared himself to Li Bo, and his contemporaries largely agreed.

sentences.zh: 嘗遊匡廬、王屋、少室諸山，留連久乃去，人莫測其意也。

translations.literal: He once traveled Mount Lu, Mount Wangwu, Mount Shaoshi, and other mountains, lingering long before departing; no one could fathom his intent.
translations.idiomatic: He once visited Mount Lu, Mount Wangwu, Mount Shaoshi, and other peaks, staying long at each before moving on, and none could guess what was in his mind.

sentences.zh: 僑居濟南，有湖山花竹之勝，作亭曰天心水面，文宗嘗敕虞集製文以記之。

translations.literal: He lived abroad in Jinan, where there was the beauty of lake, mountain, flowers, and bamboo; he built a pavilion called Heaven's Heart, Water's Surface, and Emperor Wenzong once ordered Yu Ji to compose a text to record it.
translations.idiomatic: He made his home in Jinan, where lakes, hills, flowers, and bamboo offered their charms; there he built a pavilion called Heaven's Heart, Water's Surface, and Wenzong once commanded Yu Ji to write an inscription for it.

sentences.zh: 泂尤善書，自篆、隸、草、真皆精詣，為世所珍愛。

translations.literal: Jiong was especially skilled at calligraphy; from seal, clerical, cursive, and regular scripts he attained mastery in all, and was cherished by the world.
translations.idiomatic: He was also a master of calligraphy, equally accomplished in seal, clerical, cursive, and regular scripts, and his work was treasured far and wide.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十九。

translations.literal: He died at the age of fifty-nine.
translations.idiomatic: He died at the age of fifty-nine.

sentences.zh: 有文集四十卷。

translations.literal: He left a collected works in forty juan.
translations.idiomatic: His collected works ran to forty juan.

sentences.zh: ○蘇天爵

translations.literal: ○ Su Tianjue
translations.idiomatic: Su Tianjue

sentences.zh: 蘇天爵，字伯修，真定人也。

translations.literal: Su Tianjue, courtesy name Boxiu, was a native of Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Su Tianjue, whose courtesy name was Boxiu, came from Zhending.

sentences.zh: 父志道，歷官嶺北行中書省左右司郎中，和林大饑，救荒有惠政，時稱能吏。

translations.literal: His father Zhidao served as Left and Right Department Director in the Lingbei Branch Secretariat; when Karakorum suffered great famine, his relief work showed benevolent governance, and at the time he was called a capable official.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zhidao had served as director in the left and right departments of the Lingbei Branch Secretariat; during the great famine at Karakorum his famine relief earned a reputation for humane government, and he was regarded as a capable administrator.

sentences.zh: 天爵由國子學生公試，名在第一，釋褐，授從仕郎、大都路薊州判官。

translations.literal: Tianjue, through the public examination of National University students, ranked first; upon leaving student status he was appointed Attendant Gentleman and Judge of Jizhou in the Dadu Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue took the public examination for National University students and placed first. Upon entering official service he was appointed attendant gentleman and judge of Jizhou in the Dadu circuit.

sentences.zh: 丁內外艱，服除，調功德使司照磨。

translations.literal: He observed mourning for both parents; when the mourning period ended, he was transferred to Copyist at the Merit Commission.
translations.idiomatic: After mourning for both parents he returned to service and was assigned as copyist at the Merit Commission.

sentences.zh: 泰定元年，改翰林國史院典籍官，升應奉翰林文字。

translations.literal: In the first year of Taiding, he was changed to Archivist at the Hanlin Academy National History Office, and promoted to Hanlin Attendant for Composition.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Taiding reign he became archivist at the Hanlin Academy National History Office and was promoted to Hanlin attendant for composition.

sentences.zh: 至順元年，預修《武宗實錄》。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhishun, he participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Zhishun reign he helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wuzong.

sentences.zh: 二年，升修撰，擢江南行台監察御史。

translations.literal: In the second year, he was promoted to Compiler and selected as Investigating Censor on the Jiangnan Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was promoted to compiler and appointed investigating censor on the Jiangnan branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 明年，慮囚於湖北。

translations.literal: The following year, he reviewed prisoners in Hubei.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he was sent to review prisoners in Hubei.

sentences.zh: 湖北地僻遠，民獠所雜居，天爵冒瘴毒，遍歷其地。

translations.literal: Hubei was remote and secluded, with tribal peoples intermingled in settlement; Tianjue braved malarial vapors and traveled throughout the region.
translations.idiomatic: Hubei was remote, its population mixed with tribal communities; Tianjue braved the miasma and traveled the province from end to end.

sentences.zh: 囚有言冤狀者，天爵曰：「憲司歲兩至，不言何也？」

translations.literal: When prisoners spoke of wrongful circumstances, Tianjue said: "The censorate comes twice a year—why did you not speak then?"
translations.idiomatic: When prisoners claimed they had been wronged, Tianjue asked, "The censorate visits twice a year—why did you say nothing then?"

sentences.zh: 皆曰：「前此慮囚者，應故事耳。

translations.literal: They all said: "Those who reviewed prisoners before merely followed precedent.
translations.idiomatic: They all replied, "The men who came before only went through the motions.

sentences.zh: 今聞御史至，當受刑，故不得不言。」

translations.literal: Now hearing that a censor has come, we expect to face punishment, so we cannot but speak."
translations.idiomatic: Now that a real censor has come, we expect to be punished, so we have to speak up."

sentences.zh: 天爵為之太息。

translations.literal: Tianjue sighed deeply over this.
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue sighed at the state of things.

sentences.zh: 每事必究心，雖盛暑，猶夜篝燈，治文書無倦。

translations.literal: In every matter he must probe to the heart; even in the height of summer he still lit lamps at night and handled documents without weariness.
translations.idiomatic: He pursued every case to the bottom. Even in midsummer he worked by lamplight deep into the night, handling documents without rest.

sentences.zh: 沅陵民文甲無子，育其甥雷乙，後乃生兩子，而出乙，乙俟兩子行賣茶，即舟中取斧，並斫殺之，沈斧水中，而血漬其衣，跡故在。

translations.literal: A man of Yuanling named Wen Jia had no son and raised his nephew Lei Yi; later he fathered two sons and drove Yi out. Yi waited until the two sons went out to sell tea, then took an axe from the boat and hacked both to death, sank the axe in the water, yet blood stained his clothes and the traces remained.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanling, Wen Jia had no son and raised his nephew Lei Yi. Later he had two sons of his own and sent Yi away. Yi lay in wait until the brothers went out to sell tea, took an axe from the boat, and killed them both. He threw the axe into the water, but blood had soaked his clothes and the evidence remained.

sentences.zh: 事覺，乙具服，部使者乃以三年之疑獄釋之。

translations.literal: When the affair came to light, Yi fully confessed, yet the regional commissioner released him on the grounds of a doubtful case within three years.
translations.idiomatic: When the crime was exposed Yi confessed fully, yet the regional commissioner released him as a doubtful case within the three-year statute.

sentences.zh: 天爵曰：「此事二年半耳，且不殺人，何以衣污血？

translations.literal: Tianjue said: "This affair is only two and a half years; moreover, if he did not kill anyone, how could his clothes be stained with blood?
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue said, "This case is only two and a half years old. And if he did not kill them, why was his clothing stained with blood?

sentences.zh: 又何以知斧在水中？

translations.literal: And how could he know the axe was in the water?
translations.idiomatic: How did he know the axe was in the water?

sentences.zh: 又其居去殺人處甚近，何謂疑獄？」

translations.literal: Moreover, his dwelling was very near the place of killing—what makes this a doubtful case?"
translations.idiomatic: His home stood very near the scene of the killings—what doubt is there in this case?"

sentences.zh: 遂復置於理。

translations.literal: He then had the case returned to judicial process.
translations.idiomatic: He had the case sent back for trial.

sentences.zh: 常德民盧甲、莫乙、汪丙同出傭，而甲誤墮水死，甲弟之為僧者，欲私甲妻不得，訴甲妻與乙通，而殺其夫。

translations.literal: Men of Changde named Lu Jia, Mo Yi, and Wang Bing went out together as hired laborers; Jia accidentally fell into the water and died. Jia's younger brother, who had become a monk, wished to take Jia's wife for himself but could not, and accused Jia's wife of adultery with Yi and of killing her husband.
translations.idiomatic: In Changde, Lu Jia, Mo Yi, and Wang Bing hired out together as laborers. Jia fell into the water by accident and drowned. Jia's younger brother, a monk, had wanted Jia's wife for himself; failing that, he accused her of adultery with Yi and of murdering her husband.

sentences.zh: 乙不能明，誣服擊之死，斷其首棄草間，屍與仗棄譚氏家溝中。

translations.literal: Yi could not clear himself and falsely confessed to having beaten him to death, cut off his head and abandoned it in the grass, and cast the corpse and weapon into the Tan family's ditch.
translations.idiomatic: Unable to clear himself, Yi falsely confessed to beating Jia to death, cutting off his head and leaving it in the grass, and throwing the body and weapon into the Tan family's ditch.

sentences.zh: 吏往索，果得髑髏，然屍與仗皆無有，而譚誣證曾見一屍，水漂去。

translations.literal: When clerks went to search, they indeed found a skull, yet neither corpse nor weapon was there; Tan gave false testimony that he had once seen a corpse carried away by the water.
translations.idiomatic: Officers searched and found a skull, but no body or weapon. Tan falsely testified that he had once seen a corpse carried off by the current.

sentences.zh: 天爵曰：「屍與仗縱存，今已八年，未有不腐者。」

translations.literal: Tianjue said: "Even if the corpse and weapon had remained, it is now eight years—nothing could fail to have decayed."
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue said, "Even if the body and weapon had survived, eight years have passed—nothing could remain intact."

sentences.zh: 召譚詰之，則甲未死時，目已瞽，其言曾見一屍水漂去，妄也。

translations.literal: He summoned Tan and questioned him; before Jia had died, Tan's eyes were already blind—his claim to have seen a corpse carried off by water was false.
translations.idiomatic: He summoned Tan and questioned him. Jia had still been alive when Tan went blind; his story of seeing a corpse swept away was fabrication.

sentences.zh: 天爵語吏曰：「此乃疑獄，況不止三年。」

translations.literal: Tianjue told the clerks: "This is truly a doubtful case, and moreover it exceeds three years."
translations.idiomatic: Tianjue told the officers, "This is a genuine doubtful case, and it is well beyond three years."

sentences.zh: 俱釋之。

translations.literal: He released them all.
translations.idiomatic: He released everyone involved.

sentences.zh: 其明於詳讞，大抵此類。

translations.literal: His clarity in detailed adjudication was largely of this sort.
translations.idiomatic: His mastery of close legal reasoning was largely of this kind.

sentences.zh: 入為監察御史，道改奎章閣授經郎。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Investigating Censor; en route he was changed to Lecturer at the Kui Zhang Pavilion.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled to the capital as investigating censor, but on the journey was reassigned as lecturer at the Kui Zhang Pavilion.

sentences.zh: 元統元年，復拜監察御史，在官四閱月，章疏凡四十五上，自人君至於朝廷政令、稽古禮文、閭閻幽隱，其關乎大體、系乎得失者，知無不言。

translations.literal: In the first year of Yuantong, he was again appointed Investigating Censor; during four months in office he submitted memorials forty-five times in all, from the ruler to court policies and edicts, antiquarian ritual and literature, and hidden grievances among the people—in whatever concerned the great framework or bore on gain and loss, he knew nothing he did not speak of.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Yuantong reign he was again made investigating censor. In four months he submitted forty-five memorials, touching everything from the conduct of the ruler to court policy, classical ritual, and wrongs hidden in the villages—whatever bore on the state's foundations or on success and failure, he spoke without reserve.

sentences.zh: 所劾者五人，所薦舉者百有九人。

translations.literal: Those he impeached numbered five; those he recommended numbered one hundred and nine.
translations.idiomatic: He impeached five men and recommended one hundred and nine.

sentences.zh: 明年，預修《文宗實錄》，遷翰林待制，尋除中書右司都事，兼經筵參贊官。

translations.literal: The following year, he participated in compiling the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong, was transferred to Hanlin Attending Draftsman, and soon was appointed Supervisor of Affairs in the Right Department of the Secretariat, concurrently serving as Assistant at the Classics Lectern.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he helped compile the Veritable Records of Emperor Wenzong, was promoted to Hanlin attending draftsman, and soon became supervisor of affairs in the Secretariat's right department while also serving as assistant at the classics lectern.

sentences.zh: 後至元二年，由刑部郎中改御史臺都事。

translations.literal: In the second year of Houzhiyuan, he moved from Director in the Ministry of Punishments to Supervisor of Affairs at the Censorate.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Houzhiyuan reign he moved from director in the Ministry of Punishments to supervisor of affairs at the Censorate.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷禮部侍郎。

translations.literal: In the third year, he was transferred to Vice Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: The third year he was made vice minister of rites.

sentences.zh: 五年，出為淮東道肅政廉訪使，憲綱大振，一道肅然。

translations.literal: In the fifth year, he went out as Surveillance Commissioner for Purifying Government on the Huaidong Circuit; the censorial standards were greatly revived, and the whole circuit became orderly.
translations.idiomatic: The fifth year he was sent out as surveillance commissioner for purifying government on the Huaidong circuit; discipline was sharply restored and the whole region fell into order.

sentences.zh: 入為樞密院判官。

translations.literal: He entered the capital as Vice Director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He was recalled as vice director of the Bureau of Military Affairs.

sentences.zh: 明年，改吏部尚書，拜陝西行台治書侍御史，復為吏部尚書，升參議中書省事。

translations.literal: The following year, he was changed to Minister of Personnel, appointed Investigating Censor and Secretary at the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat, again made Minister of Personnel, and promoted to Participant in the Affairs of the Secretariat Office.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he became minister of personnel, then was appointed investigating censor and secretary at the Shaanxi branch secretariat, returned to the ministry of personnel, and was promoted to participant in Secretariat affairs.

sentences.zh: 是時，朝廷更立宰相，庶務多所弛張，而天子圖治之意甚切，天爵知無不言，言無顧忌，夙夜謀畫，鬚髮盡白。

translations.literal: At this time the court had newly installed chief councillors; numerous routine affairs were slackened or stretched, yet the Son of Heaven's intent to seek good governance was very urgent; Tianjue knew nothing he did not speak of, spoke without regard for consequences, and planned day and night until his beard and hair turned entirely white.
translations.idiomatic: The court had just reshuffled its chief councillors; administration had grown lax in many areas, yet the emperor's desire for good government was keen. Tianjue spoke on everything he knew, without fear of giving offense, planning day and night until his hair and beard had turned white.

sentences.zh: 至正二年，拜湖廣行省參知政事，遷陝西行台侍御史。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhizheng, he was appointed Vice Administrator of the Huguang Branch Secretariat, then transferred to Attending Censor at the Shaanxi Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Zhizheng reign he was made vice administrator of the Huguang branch secretariat, then transferred to attending censor at the Shaanxi branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 四年，召為集賢侍講學士，兼國子祭酒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year, he was summoned as Attendant Lecturer at the Academy of Gathered Worthies, concurrently serving as Rector of the National University.
translations.idiomatic: The fourth year he was recalled as attendant lecturer at the Academy of Gathered Worthies and concurrently made rector of the National University.

sentences.zh: 天爵自以起自諸生，進為師長，端己悉心，以範學者。

translations.literal: Tianjue considered that he had risen from among the students to become their teacher and leader; he rectified himself and devoted his heart fully to set an example for scholars.
translations.idiomatic: Having risen from the ranks of students to lead them as their teacher, he disciplined himself and gave his full care to setting an example for the scholars.

sentences.zh: 明年，出為山東道肅政廉訪使，尋召還集賢，充京畿奉使宣撫。

translations.literal: The following year, he went out as Surveillance Commissioner for Purifying Government on the Shandong Circuit; soon he was recalled to the Academy of Gathered Worthies and appointed Commissioner for Pacification on a mission to the Capital Region.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was sent out as surveillance commissioner on the Shandong circuit, then soon recalled to the Academy of Gathered Worthies and appointed pacification commissioner for the capital region.

sentences.zh: 究民所疾苦，察吏之姦貪，其興除者七百八十有三事，其糾劾者九百四十有九人，都人有包、韓之譽，然以忤時相意，竟坐不稱職罷歸。

translations.literal: He investigated the people's afflictions and examined officials' corruption and greed; matters he instituted or abolished numbered seven hundred and eighty-three; persons he impeached numbered nine hundred and forty-nine; the capital's people gave him praise like that of Bao and Han, yet because he offended the chief councillor's intent, in the end he was judged unfit for office and dismissed to return home.
translations.idiomatic: He looked into the people's hardships and exposed official corruption and greed, instituting or abolishing seven hundred and eighty-three measures and impeaching nine hundred and forty-nine men. The capital compared him to Bao Xuan and Han Qi, but because he had crossed the chief councillor he was at last dismissed as unfit for office.

sentences.zh: 七年，天子察其誣，乃復起為湖北道宣慰使、浙東道廉訪使，俱未行。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, the Son of Heaven perceived that he had been slandered and therefore raised him again as Pacification Commissioner on the Hubei Circuit and Surveillance Commissioner on the Zhedong Circuit; he took neither post.
translations.idiomatic: The seventh year the emperor saw that he had been wronged and appointed him pacification commissioner for Hubei and surveillance commissioner for eastern Zhejiang, but he took neither post.

sentences.zh: 拜江浙行省參知政事。

translations.literal: He was appointed Vice Administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He was appointed vice administrator of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat.

sentences.zh: 江浙財賦，居天下十七，事務最煩劇，天爵條分目別，細巨不遺。

translations.literal: Jiangzhe's fiscal revenues accounted for seven-tenths of the realm; its affairs were the most troublesome and pressing; Tianjue divided them by category and item, omitting nothing great or small.
translations.idiomatic: Jiangzhe supplied seven-tenths of the empire's revenue and its administration was the most burdensome; Tianjue sorted every matter by category and left nothing large or small unattended.

sentences.zh: 九年，召為大都路都總管，以疾歸。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, he was summoned as Chief Administrator of the Dadu Circuit, but returned home due to illness.
translations.idiomatic: The ninth year he was summoned as chief administrator of the Dadu circuit but went home on account of illness.

sentences.zh: 俄復起為兩浙都轉運使，時鹽法弊甚，天爵拯治有方，所辦課為鈔八十萬錠，及期而足。

translations.literal: Soon he was raised again as Director-General of Transport for the Two Zhe Circuits; at the time the salt laws were greatly corrupt; Tianjue had effective methods for remedy and restoration; the revenue he handled amounted to eight hundred thousand ingots in paper money, and when the term came due it was complete.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon recalled as director-general of transport for the two Zhe circuits. The salt monopoly was then in grave disorder; Tianjue set it right with sound methods, collected eight hundred thousand ingots in paper revenue, and met the quota on schedule.

sentences.zh: 十二年，妖寇自淮右蔓延及江東，詔仍江浙行省參知政事，總兵於饒、信，所克復者，一路六縣。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year, demonic bandits spread from the right of the Huai to Jiangdong; an edict restored him as Vice Administrator of the Jiangzhe Branch Secretariat; he commanded troops at Rao and Xin; what he recovered amounted to one circuit and six counties.
translations.idiomatic: The twelfth year rebel bands spread from west of the Huai into Jiangdong. He was again made vice administrator of the Jiangzhe branch secretariat and given command at Rao and Xin; he recovered one circuit and six counties.

sentences.zh: 其方略之密，節制之嚴，雖老帥宿將不能過之。

translations.literal: The closeness of his strategy and the strictness of his discipline—even veteran commanders of long service could not surpass him.
translations.idiomatic: The tightness of his planning and the severity of his discipline surpassed even seasoned field commanders.

sentences.zh: 然以憂深病積，遂卒於軍中。

translations.literal: Yet because worry ran deep and illness accumulated, he thereupon died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: But worry and illness wore him down, and he died in camp.

sentences.zh: 年五十九。

translations.literal: He was fifty-nine years old.
translations.idiomatic: He was fifty-nine years old.

sentences.zh: 天爵為學，博而知要，長於紀載，嘗著《國朝名臣事略》十五卷、《文類》七十卷。

translations.literal: In scholarship Tianjue was broad yet knew what was essential, excelling in historical record; he once authored Outlines of Famous Ministers of Our Dynasty in fifteen juan and Literary Categories in seventy juan.
translations.idiomatic: In scholarship he was broad yet focused, especially skilled as a historian; he wrote Outlines of Famous Ministers of Our Dynasty in fifteen juan and Literary Categories in seventy juan.

sentences.zh: 其為文，長於序事，平易溫厚，成一家言，而詩尤得古法，有詩稿七卷、文稿二十卷。

translations.literal: In his literary compositions he excelled at narrative sequence, plain, gentle, and warm, forming a school of his own; in poetry he especially attained ancient methods; he had seven juan of poetic drafts and twenty juan of prose drafts.
translations.idiomatic: His prose excelled at narrative—plain, warm, and distinctive in manner—and his poetry especially preserved classical forms. He left seven juan of verse and twenty juan of prose.

sentences.zh: 於是中原前輩，凋謝殆盡，天爵獨身任一代文獻之寄，討論講辯，雖老不倦。

translations.literal: By then the senior generation of the Central Plains had withered away almost entirely; Tianjue alone bore the charge of a generation's literary heritage, discussing and debating in lecture and disputation, and though aged he did not weary.
translations.idiomatic: By then the elder scholars of the central plains had nearly all passed away, and Tianjue alone carried the literary legacy of an age, lecturing and debating without tiring even in old age.

sentences.zh: 晚歲，復以釋經為己任。

translations.literal: In his later years, he again took explicating the classics as his own duty.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years he again made explicating the classics his chief task.

sentences.zh: 學者因其所居，稱之為滋溪先生。

translations.literal: Scholars, according to where he dwelt, called him Master of Zixi Brook.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars named him for his home, calling him Master of Zixi Brook.

sentences.zh: 其他所著文，有《松廳章疏》五卷、《春風亭筆記》二卷；

translations.literal: Among his other writings were Pine Grove Memorials in five juan and Spring Breeze Pavilion Notes in two juan;
translations.idiomatic: His other writings included Pine Grove Memorials in five juan and Spring Breeze Pavilion Notes in two juan;

sentences.zh: 《遼金紀年》、《黃河原委》，未及脫稿云。

translations.literal: Chronology of Liao and Jin and Origins and Course of the Yellow River had not yet reached final draft.
translations.idiomatic: while Chronology of Liao and Jin and Origins and Course of the Yellow River were left unfinished at his death.
